The research company also expects that the successful commercialization of the dementia drug TauRx being developed by TauRx Pharmaceuticals Ltd will be a potential key factor in the valuation of Genting Bhd's stock between 1.06 and 2.64 Ringgit per share, in which Genting holds a 20% stake. It also notes that if granted a casino license in New York, the operator of the Resorts World brand integrated casino and resort, Genting Malaysia Bhd, will contribute incremental Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization (EBITDA) of 250 million to 320 million Ringgit in 2026. Based on an Ebitda enterprise value of seven times, this could further increase the valuation of the stock by 30 cents, reaching 40 cents per share. The research company stated: "We recommend investors to be positioned ahead of these potential upsides." He recommended a 'Buy' rating on Genting with a target price of RM4.75 and a target price for Malaysia Genting of RM3.30. "We like Genting because it has multi-faceted growth potential and attractive valuation, trading at an enterprise value to EBITDA multiple of 5.5 times. Genting Malaysia stands out for its high liquidity and strong 8% dividend yield. The research company stated: "The main downside risks to our 'overweight' call include lower-than-expected gaming volumes and win rates, increased gaming taxes, and value-destructive related party transactions." Philip Capital Research expects revenue growth of 24% for Genting Singapore and 18% for Genting Malaysia, driving a 21% increase in earnings by 2025 due to rising gaming volumes, non-gaming expenditures, and the steady growth in foreign and local visitation support. "Despite the strong momentum, earnings for Malaysia Genting and Genting Singapore in 2025 are projected to remain at 27% and 33% respectively, below pre-COVID-19 levels due to higher interest costs, larger losses at Resorts World (through Malaysia Genting), and higher effective tax rates." It said, "It is worth emphasizing that both companies have exceeded their Ebitda levels before the COVID-19 pandemic, which demonstrates the strength of their core business."

title: Financially undervalued, attractive dividend yield, Macau Casino stocks expected to rebound in the first half.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 3rd News) Analysts pointed out that the stock performance of Macau Casino companies lagged behind the FTSE Bursa Composite Index last year, but they believe it will gradually rebound in the first half of 2025.
Dahua Jixian stated, "We believe that the industry's profit growth, undervalued financial indicators, and attractive weekly dividend yield align very well with our potential lagging investment strategy."
"We expect profits to strengthen quarter by quarter from the fourth quarter of the 2024 fiscal year (4Q24) to the first half of 2025, mainly due to a large influx of international tourists and a strong domestic consumption trend."
This will lead to a gradual recovery in the industry's stock price in the first half of this year, but the momentum will be moderate.
According to data from the research institution, the trend of tourism consumption is still in a growth range, with consumer spending in the third quarter of 2024 increasing by 4.9% year-on-year.
Our channel survey shows that the business volume of the casino and NFO sectors remained strong between October and November 2024.
In the gambling sector, various related indicators such as flight capacity and international tourist visitation have all increased month-on-month. As for NFO, lottery sales have already recovered and stabilized at over 90% of pre-epidemic levels.
The report points out that the current valuation of the gambling industry is 1.5 to 2 standard deviations below the average level, making it highly attractive as it is still in the early stages post-epidemic.
Additionally, this industry still offers a generous weekly dividend yield ranging from 5.1% to 10.5%, benefiting from stable income and cash flow between 2024 and 2025, significantly improving compared to the low base during the epidemic.
Analysts expect that Resorts World Genting$GENTING (3182.MY)$ and Resorts World Genting Malaysia $GENM (4715.MY)$ will show improvement quarter-on-quarter in the fourth quarter of 2024, with total gambling revenue (GGR) of Resorts World Genting recovering to approximately 100% of the 2019 level.
In the third quarter of 2024, its GGR had already reached 90%.
In addition, Resorts World Genting in Malaysia has a good chance of obtaining a full casino license in southern New York, which could increase pre-tax and depreciation earnings (EBITDA) by 0.106 billion US dollars (approximately 0.47 billion Ringgit).
The investment return for TauRx is still uncertain.
As for Genting's investment in TauRx Pharmaceuticals, it remains an uncertain factor.
Genting initially invested 0.1118 billion US dollars (approximately 0.5 billion Ringgit) to acquire a 20% stake in TauRx Pharmaceuticals, and increased the investment to 0.12 billion US dollars (approximately 0.534 billion Ringgit) in 2016.
In March 2024, TauRx reported convincing 24-month Phase III clinical trial data for HMTM, a drug for Alzheimer's disease.
"Although the group has initiated regulatory processes for product approval and commercialization in the United Kingdom and the United States, we recognize that the approval and commercialization process for HMTM may take a longer time and the timeline is unclear.
"That being said, TauRx's potential valuation reaches 15 billion US dollars (approximately 66.75 billion Ringgit), which could translate to about 3.54 Ringgit per share for Genting's 20.3% stake, representing over 94% of the current market value."
Source: Nanyang Siang Pau

title: Is there any sign of the eagerly awaited tourism recovery, will Genting Singapore and Malaysia turn the tide?
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
Is there a glimpse of hope for the long-awaited tourism recovery, will Genting Sing and Malaysia see a turn for the better?
The number of Chinese tourists is recovering strongly and is now very close to pre-pandemic levels. This optimistic trend is benefiting both Genting Sing and Malaysia, both of whose businesses are experiencing a strong rebound this year.$GENTING(3182.MY)$ Due to the lackluster tourist recovery and various negative news, both Genting Sing and Malaysia's businesses are witnessing a strong rebound this year.
Amidst the less-than-ideal tourist recovery and multiple negative news, Genting Malaysia$GENM(4715.MY)$ Genting Sing$Genting Sing(G13.SG)$ The stock prices of Genting and its parent company Genting did not perform well last year, with Genting Singapore, which is listed locally, being delisted from the FTSE Conglomerates Index; while Genting Sing fell by 20% for the whole of last year.
On the other hand, after communicating with Genting Malaysia, Lion Capital International Securities learned that during the peak festive season at the end of last year, the number of Chinese tourists had significantly increased; and some casinos in Genting World reopened, coinciding with this period.
As for the business aspect in neighboring Singapore, Bloomberg Intelligence pointed out that, judging from the explosive growth in the number of flights, Genting Sing's revenue last year is expected to surpass pre-pandemic levels, reaching 102% of 2019!
Data shows that the number of tourists in Singapore for the first 11 months of 2024 increased by 22% compared to the same period last year, reaching 87% of the pre-pandemic level.
Due to a significant increase in Chinese arrivals, the total number of tourists for the year is expected to reach the upper limit of the Singapore government's target of 15 million to 16.5 million visits.
"The number of Chinese tourists alone has increased by 1.34 times year-on-year in the first 11 months."
Especially with competitors like Marina Bay Sands Hotel already fully booked, Bloomberg Intelligence is further convinced that the continuous influx of tourists will benefit Genting Sing.
Analysts also indicate that as promotional activities return to normal, it is expected that Genting Sing's profit margin in 2025 will be close to the level in 2023, further driving profit recovery.
"This indicates the gradual improvement in Genting Sing's operational efficiency and profitability, laying a solid foundation for future development."
Visa-free policies boost
Increased attractiveness of Genting Malaysia
Regarding Genting Malaysia, Lianchang International analysts also believe that the company is actively leveraging multiple bullish factors to attract tourists, especially high-spending Chinese visitors, laying the groundwork for future development.
"The extension of visa-free entry for Chinese tourists until 2026, the increase in flights between the two locations, and the upcoming 2026 Tourism Year, are all factors that enhance Genting World's appeal to Chinese visitors."
As it enters 2025, coinciding with Genting World's 60th anniversary, the company will deploy more activities and promotions to attract more visitors, further solidifying its position as a tourist hotspot.
The report points out that this series of Global Strategy indicates that Genting Malaysia is riding the market trend and policy dividends, helping to drive business growth and inject new momentum into its development.
Analysts further stated that Genting Malaysia has reopened most of the casino areas in Genting World, and has integrated digital technology, including the introduction of Electronic Table Games (ETG) and small bets, which can attract young visitors and effectively control labor costs.
With the upcoming Lunar New Year, this strategy will support first-quarter operations in 2025, achieving cost optimization during operations.
Given the recovery in tourism and the growth prospects of Genting World, analysts maintain a 'Shareholding' rating with a target price of 3.65 Ringgit.
Source: Nanyang Siang Pau

title: Rakuten Trade: New Year consumption boosts 5 major "red envelope stocks" recommended to buy on dips.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
Although the Malaysian stock market has been declining recently, as the Lunar New Year approaches, Rakuten Trade has selected 5 'Red Packet Stocks' and recommends investors to take advantage of the downturn.
Rakuten Trade's Deputy Research Director, Tang Bailin, stated at the '2025 Market Outlook' briefing today that as the Lunar New Year countdown begins, it is the peak season for festive consumption. Therefore, he has selected some consumer stocks that are expected to benefit from this trend.
In line with the Lunar New Year, he has compiled a list of 5 major 'Red Packet Stocks':
Genting Malaysia 🧧 $GENM (4715.MY)$ 🎰 - The theme park and casino will attract visitors, boosting company revenue.
Berjaya Holdings 🧧 $PADINI (7052.MY)$ 👔 - Affordable outfits benefiting from the Lunar New Year shopping spree.
Parkson Holdings 🧧 $POHKONG (5080.MY)$ 🧈 - Traditionally, Gold Trinkets, jewelry, and accessories are must-buy items for the Lunar New Year.
🧧 Heineken NV Sponsored ADR Malaysia $HEIM (3255.MY)$ 🍺 - During this period, it will boost the sales of alcoholic products.
🧧 AEON STORES $AEON (6599.MY)$🛍️ - During the Spring Festival, a wide range of popular products are provided, highly favored by individual and corporate customers.
The Shanghai Composite Index challenges 1730 points at the end of the year
In addition, Jin Bin Yoo, the trading research director of Lotte, expressed that the economic development of Malaysia in 2025 will be a highlight, especially with the recent launch of the Jusco XINJINGJI Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ).
Looking ahead, JS-SEZ will be a boost for attracting foreign direct investment (FDI), coupled with the successive announcements of large-scale domestic infrastructure projects like the Penang Light Rail Transit project, which can drive economic development.
He mentioned that the corporate profit growth in Malaysia in 2024 is impressive, with an overall expected increase of 17%. He believes that in 2025, growth is still expected to be close to 10%, and he specifically mentioned being bullish on banks and the plantation sector.
"Based on a projected P/E ratio of 16, the composite index is estimated to peak at 1730 points by the end of this year."
However, various adverse factors arising from the United States will intensify market volatility in the region.
Yoo found that prior to Trump's return to the White House, foreign funds became increasingly sensitive, especially towards negative news, further exacerbating the volatility of Malaysian and even regional stock markets.
"In the past three months, foreign funds have shifted to short-term investments, where any little disturbance may lead to withdrawals, causing the current situation where regional stock markets are below their 5-year average levels."
"However, Malaysia's political stability and positive infrastructure prospects are attracting foreign funds to a favorable position."
Trump 2.0 is expected to be more restrained.
Although Trump's measures may affect capital flows, Yu Xianbin believes that the volatility of the Trump 2.0 era is relatively mild.
He said: "Trump should be more restrained in this term. If he continues his previous thunderous style, it will only isolate the United States from the global market, which will not benefit the United States."
"Therefore, the risk in the first half of 2025 is estimated to be manageable, but as we enter the second half, the volatility of the US market may heat up."
If US inflation remains unresolved, the Fed may maintain high interest rate levels, which could impact sentiment in the second half of the year. Therefore, investors are advised to remain vigilant.
Preferred stocks for 2025
$CIMB (1023.MY)$
$GAMUDA (5398.MY)$
$MAHSING (8583.MY)$
$RHBBANK (1066.MY)$
$SUNCON (5263.MY)$
Initial public offering shares freeze liquidity for retail investors
The IPO frenzy in Malaysia in 2024 is unstoppable, with high public subscription enthusiasm causing too much funds to be 'locked up' in IPOs, greatly reducing the liquidity of retail investors, but the situation is expected to improve this year and flow into Blue Chip stocks.
Yeo Tian Bin said that Malaysia welcomed a total of 55 initial public offerings last year, raising a total amount of 7.4 billion Ringgit.
"However, the frequent influx of IPOs into the market has absorbed liquidity, especially the liquidity of secondary small-cap stocks."
"Although we consider the fundraising amount of IPOs to be at a healthy level, the surge in oversubscription is causing concern."
Among them, Steel Eagle, which moved to the GEM last year, $HAWK (0320.MY)$ achieved an oversubscription ratio of 2.77 times.
Due to retail investors' excessive enthusiasm for IPO activities, a large amount of funds from this category of investors were locked up, leading to a decrease in market participation, dropping to a low of 16% in September last year.
"Nevertheless, Yeo Tian Bin believes that this year the situation of retail funds being 'locked up' will improve, and these funds will continue to circulate in the market without any major sell-offs."
"Over time, it is expected that retail investors will see net inflows, ideally flowing towards blue-chip stocks to boost the performance of the composite index."
Source: Nanyang Siang Pau

After a year of hard work and effort, those billionaires standing at the top of the business wave have delivered an impressive answer sheet. Under the wave of Datacenter in Malaysia, institutions in the Technology and construction sectors focusing on this field have repeatedly proven their influence with strength.
Among them, Yang Zhongli, who first seized the AI wave in our country, saw their stock prices soar for two consecutive years; this has caused the group's leader, Tan Sri Yang Subin, and family wealth to increase annually, placing them in the top three of the Malaysian billionaire list.
As of the end of 2024, Yang Subin and his family's wealth has surged by 7 billion Ringgit compared to the previous year, reaching 21.5 billion Ringgit. His position on the billionaire list has thus improved from 5th place a year ago to 3rd place.
Moreover, the Yang family is now not far from the top two billionaires in our country. This is mainly because our country's perennial richest man, Guo Heniang, and Tan Sri Guan Baoqiang, who has ranked second on the billionaire list for four consecutive years, have both experienced a shrinkage in wealth over the past year.
However, Yang Subin seems to be starting the year poorly in 2025. With the USA implementing restrictions on AI Chip and the free coupon red envelopes not being well-received by the market, within less than a month into the year, the Yang brothers have already faced two waves of drastic declines. It remains uncertain whether the Yang family can continue to turn risks into opportunities and shine again in 2025.
Besides the Yang family making a strong entry into the top three, the 2024 Nanyang Rich List also witnessed the emergence of Sunway. $SUNWAY (5211.MY)$ Founder and Group Chairman Tan Sri Cheah Fook Ling saw his wealth surge by over 10 billion Ringgit within a year. $99SMART (5326.MY)$ After its listing, the founder Li Liang Hua of 99 Speed Mart revealed his wealth, making a strong entrance into Malaysia's top ten richest list with a net worth of 17.6 billion Ringgit.
The wealth of Malaysia's top 40 tycoons surged by 45.9 billion Ringgit, challenging Robert Kuok's position as the richest man.
The year 2024 is a good year for Malaysian stocks. After experiencing three years of decline, the Malaysian stocks finally flourished in the Year of the Dragon, with the FTSE Bursa Malaysia Conglomerates Index rising nearly 13% throughout the year. In such favorable conditions, Malaysia's billionaires naturally seized the opportunity, with the total wealth of the top 40 billionaires increasing by 45.9 billion Ringgit or 19.3%, reaching a total of 306.9 billion Ringgit.
Among them, without a doubt, once again reigning as Malaysia's richest person is the 'Sugar King' Robert Kuok. However, over the past year, as his assets across Malaysia, Singapore, and Hong Kong have shrunk, Robert Kuok's wealth has decreased by over 2.5 billion Ringgit, falling below 30 billion Ringgit, with a 'remaining' fortune of 28.57 billion Ringgit.
Compared to Robert Kuok's peak wealth, this now represents almost a halving! In 2017, his net worth soared to 49.9 billion Ringgit, but in recent years, due to the devastation of the pandemic and a decline in the Chinese consumer market where he focuses, the Sugar King's wealth fell to 31.1 billion Ringgit last year and has further declined this year.
That being said, Robert Kuok has still maintained the title of richest person for many years, primarily because of Qi Li, who ranks second on China's billionaire list. $PMETAL (8869.MY)$ The total wealth of CEO Tan Sri Kuan Bo Chiang and his family also saw a decline last year.
The two top tycoons of the billionaire list encountered a setback.
In 2024, Qi Li's performance was actually not too bad. Global aluminum prices and Qi Li's performance both increased, but unfortunately, the stock price performance was not particularly outstanding, with a yearly increase of 1.9%, which is quite unsatisfactory compared to the overall market.
For the Kuan family, the main culprit for their wealth not increasing but instead declining is their other aluminum products manufacturer, Qi Li Technology. $PMBTECH (7172.MY)$ Due to significant fluctuations in performance and being overvalued, Qi Li Technology's stock plummeted by 35% last year.
This consequently led to the Kuan family's wealth being recorded at 23.59 billion Ringgit, a slight decline of 0.06 billion Ringgit or 0.3%, allowing them to maintain the second position on the billionaire list.
在管保强与家族之后，杨忠礼机构 $YTL (4677.MY)$ 的掌门人丹斯里杨肃斌与家族的财富正在高速增长，如今以21.5 billion令吉的身家坐上了2024南洋富豪榜探花的位置，对前两名发起了强烈的
群雄争霸
与此同时，富豪榜的大黑马，分别执掌IOI集团 $IOICORP (1961.MY)$与IOI置业 $IOIPG (5249.MY)$ 的拿督李耀祖和李耀昇在经过多年的稳健爬升之后，财富突破了20 billion令吉，以20.3 billion令吉身家，位居我国第4富豪的位置。
追溯历史，在李耀祖和李耀昇兄弟接掌之前，IOI集团的创办人，已故丹斯里李深静，曾在2017年身家突破20 billion令吉；但在李深静逝世之后，IOI集团陷入了短暂的悲痛与动荡当中。如今，李氏兄弟的身家重新返回20 billion令吉以上，完美地证明了虎父无犬子。
In 2024, there are a total of 4 billionaires in the country with a net worth exceeding 20 billion Ringgit, but in the new year, the competition at the top of the billionaire list is not limited to these 4 individuals, as the 5th ranked billionaire, from Sunway, $SUNWAY (5211.MY)$ Tan Sri Cheah Fook Nien, is only a whisker away from the top ranks.
Cheah Fook Nien's total net worth reaches 19.96 billion Ringgit in 2024, just a step away from the 20 billion threshold! Don't forget, Sunway's Medical business may go public within the next couple of years, at which point, it is believed he will bring a new impact to our country's billionaire list!
The new waves push the old waves.
In contrast, the 6th place in the billionaire list, the late Tan Sri Cheng Hong Biao, although his wealth is also infinitely close to the 20 billion threshold at 19.72 billion Ringgit, with the Cheng family having clarified the method of inheritance distribution, including gradually reducing their shareholding in Public Bank $PBBANK (1295.MY)$ to below 10%, it is expected that Cheng Hong Biao and his descendants will gradually lose competitiveness in the future Nanyang billionaire list, and the situation of once being ranked second in the Malaysian billionaire list can only become a memory.
However, the billionaire list is often like this, the old waves have not yet receded, the new waves have already rushed in. Following Cheng Hong Biao, ranked 7th in the 2024 Nanyang billionaire list, is last year's brightest new wave, the founder and CEO of 99 Speed Mart, Li Lianghua.
After 99 Speed Mart went public last September, the stock price has been soaring, and within just three months it made its way into the Blue Chip category. This propelled Li Lianghua to land at 7th place on the billionaire list with a net worth of 17.6 billion Ringgit.
Lin Guotai has dropped out of the top ten.
In the 2024 Nanyang Rich List, besides Li Lianghua who parachuted in at the 7th position, the changes in the top ten richest individuals in our country are minimal. At the 8th position is Datuk Seri Dr. Khoo Kay Peng, the founder of Hong Leong Group, whose wealth has increased, but due to stronger performances by other billionaires, his ranking has dropped by 2 places.
As for the 9th-ranked Xie Songkun and his family, as well as the 10th-ranked late Ananda Krishnan, their wealth changes in 2024 are not substantial, and they have maintained their positions among the top ten richest in our country.
As for the one who was "kicked out" of the top ten billionaires by Li Lianghua, it is Datuk Lim Goh Tong from Genting Group. Over the past few years, Genting's businesses around the world seem to have faced continuous setbacks, with the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic still lingering on the global tourism industry, which has not fully recovered, and after years of decline, the once Malaysian Star Stock Genting $GENTING (3182.MY)$ and Resorts World Genting Malaysia $GENM (4715.MY)$ , has now been removed from the FTSE Bursa Malaysia Conglomerates Index.
Consequently, Lim Kuo Tai's wealth has also repeatedly decreased. After losing 1.25 billion Ringgit last year, his net worth is now less than 8 billion Ringgit, ranking him 14th.
In addition to Lim Kuo Tai, there are several other notable figures outside the top ten, who have previously made headlines in the Nanyang Wealth Rankings. For example, Asia's Mercedes tycoon Tan Sri Lau Chu Kuan has a fate very similar to Lim Kuo Tai in the wealth rankings. $HAPSENG (3034.MY)$ The company he leads, Synthesia, has been expelled from the Blue Chip ranks after continuous stock price declines; his position on the wealth list has also slipped to 17th.
Former top wealth holders sharing the same fate.
Also experiencing a continued decline is the late Cambodian gambling king, Tan Sri Cheng Lek. Cheng Lek once ranked second in the Nanyang Wealth list, but after his death in 2023, disputes over inheritance arose among his descendants, which significantly reduced his wealth, currently placing him 18th with approximately 5.2 billion Ringgit.
Outside the top ten, there is another former runner-up in the Malaysian wealth rankings, He Te Jia. $HARTA (5168.MY)$ Executive Chairman Kwan Kim An. However, this former second richest person in Malaysia, unlike Lim Kuo Tai and Cheng Lek, has passed the low point and is seeing a recovery in wealth.
The glove tycoon enjoys a sweet return after the hardships.
Actually, it is not just Guan Jin'an; in the past year, the glove tycoons in the country finally reaped the rewards of their hard work. Since the pandemic, glove stocks have experienced both peak periods of immense prosperity and low valleys of being scorned. Fortunately, in 2024, most glove manufacturers have turned losses into profits, causing stock prices to rise significantly, and the net worth of glove tycoons has also seen a substantial increase.
As a result, Guan Jin'an's wealth increased by 46% last year, reaching 6.7 billion Ringgit, ranking 13th and launching a renewed bid for the top 10; while Top Glove's $TOPGLOV (7113.MY)$ Tan Sri Lim Wee Chai, from High Productivity Latex Products, $KOSSAN (7153.MY)$ as well as the brothers from the Singapore-listed glove company Riverstone, Huang Deshun, all saw their fortunes rise by over 40% last year.
Struggle for Supremacy
In 2024, outside the top 20 rankings of the Nanyang Rich List, as usual, it is a fierce competition, with little wealth disparity among the major tycoons. A slight shift in the market sentiment in related fields could significantly impact the rankings of the rich list.
For example, our Technology stocks experienced a rocky journey last year. In general, the performance of Technology stocks in the past year has not been ideal, leading to a notable decline in the wealth of several tech tycoons, and consequently, their rankings also dropped significantly.
The ranking of tech tycoons has significantly fallen.
Among these, the biggest drop belongs to the leaders of Di & Hong and Wu Nanhua and his family. $D&O (7204.MY)$With the global car market cooling down, Di & Hong, which mainly produces automotive semiconductors, could not escape the downturn. The stock price fell by 42% over the year, resulting in a reduction of 0.54 billion Ringgit in Wu Nanhua and his family's wealth last year.
Meanwhile, UWC's executive director and group CEO, Datuk Huang Chai Rong, along with executive director Liu Jiqiang, are also facing similar difficulties. $UWC (5292.MY)$ The company's stock price dropped by more than 10% last year, leading to a shrinkage of 0.26 billion Ringgit in the wealth of the two founders.
This has made the above two groups some of the richest individuals experiencing the most significant drop in the 2024 Nanyang Rich List. Wu Nanhua's ranking fell 9 places to 32nd, with wealth of 2.72 billion Ringgit; Huang Chai Rong and Liu Jiqiang also dropped 9 places to 36th, with wealth of 2.31 billion Ringgit.
Another tech tycoon who has emerged in recent years, Datuk Chen Rongqi, CEO of Ge Dais Technology, shares a similar fate. $GREATEC (0208.MY)$ Last year, his wealth shrank by 0.34 billion Ringgit, and he dropped 7 places in the wealthy list, ranking 27th with a wealth of 3.37 billion Ringgit.
Of course, not every technology stock and tech tycoon has gone through a bitter year; some tech stocks performed well last year due to their business related to the booming datacenters in recent years.
For example, the newcomer king of the 2023 rich list, NationGate Holdings. $NATGATE (0270.MY)$ Executive Director Huang Yongliang has become more and more courageous in his second year on the list, with wealth increasing by over 1 billion Ringgit, now having a fortune of 3.27 billion Ringgit, rising to the 28th position on the rich list.
Three property tycoons have re-entered the list.
On the other hand, over the past year, the construction and property stocks in the country have revived, with Kerjaya being the most typical representative. $KERJAYA (7161.MY)$Datuk Seri Zheng Ronghe has seen his wealth increase by 67% in the past year, and his ranking has climbed to the 23rd position.
At the same time, three billionaires who previously made the Nanyang rich list but whose property stocks performed poorly in recent years, including Datuk Seri Chen Runchuan of Dengkang Holdings. $TANCO (2429.MY)$ Datuk Liang Guohua of Green Prosperity. $ECOWLD (8206.MY)$ and Qiaofeng Holdings. $OSK (5053.MY)$Tan Sri Huang Zonghua has successfully returned to the list of the top 40 billionaires.
The 40th richest person in our country in 2024 is MyEG. $MYEG (0138.MY)$ The Managing Director, Huang Tian Shun, has a wealth of 2.21 billion Ringgit, significantly raising the entry threshold for the Nanyang Rich List by over 30%. In 2023, the entry threshold for the Nanyang Rich List was only 1.69 billion Ringgit.

title: Foreign selling pressure caused a sharp decline in AI concept stocks, with Malaysian stocks having their worst start in 30 years in January.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
According to statistics, January 2025 became the worst start of the year for the Malaysian stock market in 30 years, mainly due to the impact of large-scale foreign sell-offs.
Lian Chang International pointed out today in a research report that the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI fell by 5% month-on-month in January, marking the most severe January decline since 1995.
Foreign investors sold off a net amount of up to 3.1 billion Ringgit of Malaysian stocks in January, the highest monthly foreign outflow since 2020.
Due to the impact of the tightening of advanced semiconductor exports from the United States, AI and Datacenter concept stocks have been hit hard. In addition, the recent rise of the Chinese AI startup DeepSeek has also intensified market uncertainty.
The targets of foreign sell-offs are mainly concentrated in the utilities and property sectors, which together account for more than one-third of the total net outflow.
Looking at the industry indices, the Construction Index performed the worst, while the Property/A-REIT Index counter-intuitively rose by 0.4%.
At the same time, local institutional investors took advantage of the situation and bought a total of 1.23 billion Ringgit worth of stocks. Retail investors also net bought 1.2 billion Ringgit.
There is a turnaround in February.
However, Lion Chan International believes that based on historical data, the Malaysian stock market usually performs more positively in February.
Due to the selling wave in January, the valuation of the Long Index is currently lower than its five-year average P/E ratio level, providing investors with an opportunity to "buy on dips".
Historical data shows that the Long Index has an average ROI of 0.8% in February over the past 10 years, reaching 2.2% over the past 47 years.
The bank maintains the SSE Conglomerates Index target of 1763 points, with preferred investment stocks including:
• Tianditong Digital Network $CDB (6947.MY)$ • Fung Lung Bank $HLBANK (5819.MY)$ • Gold Affairs $GAMUDA (5398.MY)$ National Energy $TENAGA (5347.MY)$ Genting Malaysia $GENM (4715.MY)$
February Focus Events:
The 15th Parliament Session (until March 6th) MSCI Index Adjustment Results (February 11th) Release of 4th Quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP) for 2024 (February 14th) Corporate Earnings Season and Updates on US Trade Policies Impact of Minimum Wage of 1700 Ringgit Impact of a 2% foreign employee provident fund rate
Trade war sparks safe-haven demand and gold price hits a new record high
In addition, the gold price rose to a record high, rising nearly 1% in the previous trading day, as the new round of trade war between the United States and China sparked safe-haven demand.
On Wednesday, gold touched a record high of $2848.27 per ounce.
The day before, U.S. President Trump officially imposed a 10% tariff on Chinese goods exported to the U.S., prompting Beijing to take rapid but more targeted retaliatory actions.
A weaker U.S. dollar index on Tuesday made gold more affordable for many buyers, as the index extended its decline after the U.S. employment report showed a gradual slowdown in the labor market.
US-China tariff war begins, Trump: No hurry to talk to Xi Jinping
U.S. President Trump stated that he is not in a rush to talk to Chinese President Xi Jinping, despite expectations that they will hold discussions after the intensified tariff measures in the escalating trade conflict.
According to comprehensive foreign media reports, Trump had previously stated that he might have a dialogue with Xi Jinping early this week, but on the afternoon of the 4th at the White House, he told reporters that he was 'not in a hurry' to speak with Xi Jinping.
White House Press Secretary Levitt also stated on the 3rd that Trump would speak with Xi Jinping, but she said the next day that there was currently no 'latest news on when the two will have a call'.
Outside the West Wing office of the White House, Levitt told reporters: 'He (Trump) will not allow China to continue to produce and distribute deadly fentanyl to the United States. That is the reason for imposing tariffs.'
Levitt stated that the call between Trump and Xi Jinping still needs to be arranged. She said: 'President Xi did indeed make contact with President Trump to discuss this matter, perhaps to start negotiations, so we await further developments.'
Similar to the dialogue between Trump and the leaders of Mexico and Canada on the 3rd, the dialogue between the leaders of the United States and China is seen as a key to possibly reducing or postponing the imposition of tariffs.
Shortly after Trump's threat to impose a 10% tariff on Chinese goods took effect on the 4th, Beijing announced tariffs on imported products such as US energy, autos, and agricultural machinery. In addition, China also issued a notice to companies including Google, warning of possible sanctions, in cautious response to Trump's tariff war.
When asked about retaliatory tariffs from China, Trump said at the White House: 'It doesn't matter.'
After Canada and Mexico pledged to strengthen actions to block fentanyl and undocumented immigrants from crossing into the United States, Trump postponed the date for imposing tariffs on Canada and Mexico to March 1st on the 3rd.
As the trade war reignites, the Renminbi remains relatively strong.
China welcomes the first trading day after the Spring Festival holiday. In the midst of the reignition of the trade war, the People's Bank of China slightly strengthened the midpoint, continuing the stability-oriented stance before the holiday, reflecting the foreign exchange rate policy still prioritizing stability.
The onshore exchange rate fell to a weak 7.28 yuan, slightly weaker than the offshore rate by less than a hundred points, with a generally stable trend.
On Wednesday, the Renminbi midpoint rate was marginally raised by 5 points to 7.1693 yuan compared to pre-holiday levels, maintaining a stronger bias of 1120 points above market forecast averages.
During the Spring Festival holiday closure of the onshore market, the offshore Renminbi experienced significant fluctuations, falling to 7.3734 yuan at one point on Monday, approaching the historical low of 7.3749 yuan set in 2022.
"The midpoint rate today is a clear signal, indicating that regulators currently have no intention of letting the Renminbi exchange rate weaken," said Wu Kun, Director of Asia Research at the ANZ Bank in Singapore, in an interview.
He mentioned that in the face of a 10% tariff hike imposed by the US, regulators seem to believe that the leaders of China and the US could reach some form of agreement in the next few days, hence keeping the midpoint rate stable.
After the announcement of the midpoint rate, the offshore Renminbi remains generally stable. The offshore Renminbi trend is flat, at 7.2868 yuan.
The onshore Renminbi saw a slight decline at the opening, with a magnitude of nearly 0.4%, at 7.2810 yuan, calculated based on today's midpoint price. The intraday devaluation limit price is at 7.3127 yuan.
Maintaining balanced and repairing relationships – China's trade concessions are drawing attention.
Jo Hong, Chief Economist of BofA Securities Greater China, stated that the form of future agreements will depend on the concessions that China may agree to make.
She believes that China's options include committing to purchase more US oil and gas, maintaining the stability of the Renminbi exchange rate, and fulfilling the commitments of the Phase One trade agreement, a combination of these measures may help repair the relationship between the two countries.
Chang Shuang, Chief Asian Economist of Bloomberg Economics Research, mentioned that China's influence over the Panama Canal can be a card played by Trump.
A Hong Kong company owns two of the five ports near the Panama Canal, the Trump administration threatened that if Panama does not reduce China's influence, the US will take back the canal.
Shuang predicted that China may exert pressure on this subsidiary of CKH Holdings to reduce its local business, but he believes this possibility is very slim.
According to sources, Panama is weighing whether to cancel contracts with the subsidiary of CKH.
These unnamed sources cautioned that no decision has been made at the moment, and the government will act to avoid litigation and follow due process.
Joseph, a professor of international relations at East China Normal University in Shanghai, said that the Chinese government is taking a balanced approach, wanting to appear strong while not escalating.
Trade War 2.0 Causes Market Turbulence, Large High-Dividend Stocks Serve as Safe Havens
Amid the uncertainty brought by the trade war, investors may prefer to seek large high-dividend stocks to mitigate risks.
According to Bloomberg's data, on the Malaysia Stock Exchange, there are large cap stocks exceeding 10 billion Ringgit, including Genting Malaysia and Industrial Bank, with a weekly dividend yield above 5%. $GENM (4715.MY)$ , Sinarmas $SIME (4197.MY)$ and Industrial Bank $RHBBANK (1066.MY)$ have a weekly yield rate exceeding 5%.
Among them, Genting Malaysia has the highest dividend yield at 7.1%, followed by Sunway at 6.55%, and Industrial Bank at 6.26%.
Since being excluded from the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index in December last year, Genting Malaysia's stock price has fallen by 20% cumulatively, also one of the reasons for its high weekly yield.
Financial website TheEdge reported that Hui Li Capital Research Director Chen Jianyuan (translated pronunciation) believes that with the expected improvement in Genting Malaysia's free cash flow, the company's dividend for 2025 may increase.
Furthermore, if Genting Malaysia successfully obtains a New York casino license (expected to be announced by the end of the year), its stock price is likely to receive a catalyst for re-rating.
In the banking sector, Industrial Bank currently has the highest weekly yield, reaching 6.26%. Chen Jianyuan pointed out that Industrial Bank is well capitalized, with a Tier 1 capital ratio of 16.6%, hence it has the ability to increase dividends.
Melaka Securities research director Liu Liyu prefers Malayan Banking Berhad, due to its stable market position in the Malaysian banking industry. $MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ Chen Jianyuan also agrees with this view, as he believes that Malayan Banking Berhad provides a good opportunity for bottom fishing amidst recent softening stock prices, making it a safe haven choice in the current market volatility.
He believes that the recent softening of Malayan Banking Berhad's stock price provides a good opportunity to accumulate at lower levels, making it a safe haven choice amidst market fluctuations.
According to Bloomberg, Sime Darby's dividend per share is expected to increase by 10.8% in 2025, making it the company with the largest increase among large-cap stocks. This growth is mainly attributed to Sime Darby's acquisition of UMW in March last year, further expanding its business foundation.

rich_text.text: According to statistics, January 2025 became the worst performing first month of the year for Malaysian stocks in 30 years, mainly due to significant foreign selling pressure.
In a research report today, Lion Fund Composite Index fell by 5% in January compared to the previous month, marking the most severe January decline since 1995.
Foreign investors sold a net 3.1 billion ringgit of Malaysian stocks in January, the highest monthly net outflow of foreign funds since 2020.

Due to the impact of the tightening of advanced semiconductor exports by the USA, AI and datacenter concept stocks have been hit hard. In addition, the recent rise of Chinese AI startup DeepSeek has also heightened market uncertainty.
Foreign funds mainly targeted utility and property sectors for selling, with these two sectors accounting for more than one-third of the total net outflow.
Looking at industry indexes, the construction index performed the worst, while the industrial REITs index bucked the trend with a slight increase of 0.4%.

At the same time, local institutional investors took the opportunity to accumulate, buying a total of 1.23 billion Ringgit worth of stocks, while retail investors also had a net purchase of 1.2 billion Ringgit.
There is a turning point in February.
However, Lion Global International believes that based on historical data, Malaysian stocks tend to perform positively in February.
Due to the selling wave in January, the current valuation of the LFP Composite Index is lower than its five-year average P/E ratio level, providing investors with an opportunity to "buy on dips."
Historical data shows that the LFP Composite Index has had an average return rate of 0.8% in February over the past 10 years, and it reached 2.2% over the past 47 years.

title: [Exclusive/Nanyang Rich List] Lim Kok Thay has fallen out of the top ten, and Technology tycoons are all in decline.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
Exclusive Report:@Jungle lee
Initially, 2024 was expected to be a bountiful year of "Dragon Roaring in the Sky," but reality turned out to be contrary. Gambling and Technology stocks became the biggest losers, with stock prices continuously falling, and there is almost no hope of a rebound.
Notably, the head of Malaysian gambling giant Genting (GENTING, 3182, Main Board Consumer Stocks), Tan Sri Lim Guohai, who has long held a place in the top ten of the Nanyang Rich List, saw a significant reduction in wealth in 2024, unexpectedly falling out of the top ten rankings, shocking the market.
Will 2025 bring a turning point of "Snake All Beautiful"? Finding a way to stage a spectacular comeback has become a common expectation of the market and investors.
Follow the footsteps of the 'Nanyang Siang Pau' to uncover the rise and fall of Gambling and Technology Stocks in the '2024 Nanyang Rich List'.
The stock prices of Genting siblings have plummeted.
Lim Kuo Tai's wealth evaporated by 16%.
In 2024, Malaysia's Gambling Industry faces a difficult moment, Genting. $GENTING (3182.MY)$ and Genting Malaysia. $GENM (4715.MY)$ are undoubtedly at the eye of the storm, unable to extricate themselves.
The sharp decline in stock prices and shrinking Market Cap not only caused the Genting siblings to fall out of the FTSE Bursa Malaysia Composite Index constituent stocks list, but also directly affected the personal wealth of the group's helm, Genting Chairman and CEO Tan Sri Lim Kuo Tai.
As of the end of December, Genting Group's Market Cap has fallen to 15 billion Ringgit, ranking 34th in the Malaysian stock market, while Genting Malaysia stands at 13.4 billion Ringgit, ranking 37th.
This dismal performance has caused the share prices of the Genting duo to plummet from their peak, especially for Genting Malaysia, whose stock price has dropped from 6 Ringgit in 2017 to 2.26 Ringgit by the end of 2024.
Lim Kok Thay's wealth has also evaporated by nearly 16%, making him one of the personalities with the most severe decline in the 2024 Nanyang Rich List.
The accumulation of multiple adverse factors is the main reason that has led the Genting duo into trouble.
From the dispute regarding the 20th Century Fox theme park in 2018, to the gambling tax increase in 2019, and the severe impact of the pandemic on the tourism industry in 2020, Genting Group's profitability has been long constrained.
Additionally, the recent intensification of global economic uncertainty and tightening liquidity in the Capital Markets have caused investors to lose confidence in the Gambling industry.
$Genting Sing (G13.SG)$
The overall Gambling industry remains sluggish.
In 2024, while Genting World's gambling revenue has returned to 90% of the 2019 level, the overall performance of the industry is still sluggish, with market sentiment deeply affected by the adjustments of component stocks.
Analysts point out that the valuation of the Genting Twins has dropped to a historical low, which is 1.5 to 2 standard deviations below the average.
However, ongoing negative news and uncertainty keep investors cautious.
To make matters worse, Genting Malaysia is being sued by its partner at RW Bimini in the Bahamas for alleged accounting fraud, seeking $0.6 billion (approximately 2.575 billion Ringgit) in damages.
The company's wholly-owned U.S. subsidiary, Genting Americas (GAI), was sued by RAV Bahamas Ltd. (RAV) on October 7, 2024, local time, in the Federal District Court for the Southern District of Florida, with the lawsuit notification served to GAI on October 11.
The statement mentions that the lawsuit involves operational matters related to RW Bimini, with RAV claiming over $0.6 billion in damages.
Worse still, Genting Sing's predicament worsens, as analysts downgrade its stock rating due to poor earnings, causing the stock price to drop to a two-year low.
Is rebirth in adversity the way back to glory?
In the face of adversity, Lim Kook Thai and the management team are seeking breakthroughs, looking towards 2025, planning to diversify their business and gradually revive their core Gambling business to restore market confidence, with the return of international tourists and growth in domestic consumption likely to be key drivers.
Analysts predict that the Gambling Industry will fully rebound in profitability by the first half of 2025, with Genting Malaysia's gambling revenue expected to return to 2019 levels.
In addition, the progress of Genting Malaysia's application for a full casino license in New York, USA, is also attracting attention, as success in this endeavor would add 0.47 billion Ringgit to the group's annual EBITDA, greatly enhancing profitability.
Meanwhile, the UK pharmaceutical company TauRx, in which Genting holds a 20.33% stake, is seen as a major potential growth point.
Its Alzheimer’s drug - HMTM, is currently advancing through the approval and commercialization process, and TauRx has a potential valuation of up to 15 billion USD, which, if progress goes smoothly, could bring a potential value of 3.54 Ringgit per share to Genting.
As for its subsidiary, Resorts World Las Vegas (RWLV), to restore the company's reputation, a new board of directors was announced at the end of December last year to shake off the stigma of alleged involvement in money laundering activities.
Will things go as smoothly as expected?
Of course, the road to recovery will not be as smooth as anticipated, as there are uncertainties regarding the New York state casino license, the protracted cycle of TauRx's commercialization, and potential fluctuations in the overall economic environment, all of which are challenges that need to be overcome.
Analysts warn that despite the attractive high dividend yields and low valuations of Genting's dual entities, the likelihood of a significant rebound in stock prices in the short term is low.
Lin Guotai and Genting Group's ability to reverse the situation by 2025 will become a focus of market attention.
After gradually digesting the negative factors, the Genting duo may welcome a moderate recovery. However, whether they can survive and make breakthroughs in adversity will depend on the effectiveness of their Business diversification strategy and the recovery speed of their core Gambling business.
US technology stocks continue to hit record highs.
The new Malaysian tech giants are facing a decline.
While US technology stocks set new highs in 2024, the Malaysian Technology Sector is mired in difficulties, with continuously poor stock performance, disappointing the market.
This phenomenon breaks the historical trend of a high positive correlation between global Semiconductors sales and the Malaysian Technology Sector, showing a reverse relationship.
What are the reasons behind this change? Looking ahead to 2025, can the Malaysian Technology field welcome dawn? Will Trump's return have potential impacts?
Looking at the '2024 Nanyang Rich List', it is not difficult to see that the tycoons involved in the Technology Sector are all facing a significant wealth depletion issue.
Among them, the helm of Meijia First. $MFCB (3069.MY)$ And the Emperor and Hong. $D&O (7204.MY)$ Wu Nanhua and his family experienced a decline in wealth of 0.5 billion Ringgit or 17%, falling from 23rd place in 2023 to 32nd place.
Although Meijia First is involved in a large number of renewable Energy Assets and has successfully climbed the Datacenter train, its stock price rose 24% for the year, however, Emperor and Hong had no such luck, with a stock price trend opposite to Meijia First, plummeting 42%.
This drop is enough to pull down Wu Nanhua and his family's wealth ranking by 9 positions.
Additionally, other technology tycoons facing declines in wealth include UWC company. $UWC (5292.MY)$ Executive Director and Group CEO Dato' Huang Cairong and Liu Jiqiang, whose billionaire ranking fell from 27th to 36th, with a wealth decline of 0.26 billion Ringgit or 10.1%, coming to 2.31 billion Ringgit.
As for Ge Dai Technology. $GREATEC (0208.MY)$ The overall CEO, Datuk Chen Rongqi, also performed poorly, with his ranking dropping from 20th to 27th, and his wealth decreased by 0.34 billion Ringgit, or 9.2%, to 3.37 billion Ringgit.
Trump becomes a new variable.
In fact, the external market is filled with many uncertainties, and Trump's policies may once again affect the performance of Global technology stocks.
Potential bullish opportunities include Trump's possible continuation of his 'America First' policy, which could drive investment and growth in USA businesses, thus boosting the technology sector in USA stocks. Some Malaysian technology companies, as part of the Global supply chain, may have the opportunity to benefit indirectly from the expansion of demand in the USA market.
The potential risk is that Trump may restart the tariff policies on products from China or strengthen protectionism in the technology sector, thus intensifying the technology competition between China and USA, disrupting the Global supply chain, and putting pressure on Malaysian technology stocks that are highly dependent on international markets.
Of course, the slowdown in Global auto sales and the frequent release of weak earnings reports by European luxury car brands have made investors adopt a more cautious attitude towards companies related to automotive technology semiconductors.
In Malaysia's Technology Sector, companies such as DNB and Tenda Technology, $PENTA (7160.MY)$ The Pacific, $MPI (3867.MY)$ and others have recently seen their performance impacted.
In contrast, there are very few companies benefiting from the AI sector. $FRONTKN (0128.MY)$ Among them, Frontline Technology has performed the best, with its client Taiwan Semiconductor directly benefiting from NVIDIA's continued strength.
Taiwan Semiconductor's latest performance shows a net profit growth of 57% year-on-year, and it is expected that revenue will further increase by 25% in 2025.
With the halo effect of AI, Frontline Technology's stock price broke the historical high of 4.78 Ringgit in July 2024. Although future performance looks bullish, the risk of overvaluation should not be ignored, and investors need to remain cautious in their planning.
The recovery is still full of uncertainty.
Despite the Malaysian Technology Index declining for two consecutive years, it edged up 2.5% to 64.89 points by the end of 2024, but started poorly in 2025, dropping nearly 6%.
US economic data exceeded expectations, and the Federal Reserve's potential pause on interest rate cuts or even a return to rate hikes further pressured the performance of overvalued companies.
Additionally, the recovery path for Malaysian Technology companies is not smooth.
Packaging and testing companies such as Inari Amertron $INARI (0166.MY)$ , Mat Pacific $MPI (3867.MY)$ , Unison $UNISEM (5005.MY)$ have all seen their stock prices drop to a one-year low this year, reflecting market's short-term lack of confidence in this sector.
Facing uncertainties in outside markets and the complex environment with "madman Trump" returning to politics, investors may need to shift their focus rather than concentrate on individual sectors.
The limitation of the Technology Sector in Malaysia is that the majority of companies are concentrated in the mid to downstream fields, such as backend packaging testing and electronic assembly, lacking upstream chip design capabilities.
NVIDIA holds a dominant position.
Although AI has driven Global semiconductor sales, this growth is mainly concentrated in the USA market, with NVIDIA contributing a significant proportion.
It is worth mentioning that global semiconductor sales are expected to grow by 12.5% in 2025, reaching 687 billion USD (approximately 3.1 trillion Ringgit), but when excluding NVIDIA's revenue, Global semiconductor sales are actually stagnant.
This further highlights the importance of top companies and the structural opportunities in the field of AI.
Looking back at Malaysia, most tech companies are still focused on the fields of communication, Smart Phones, Autos, and industrial sectors.
However, the slowdown in Smart Phone shipment growth, along with massive layoffs in the automotive sector, all reflect weak demand for end products, and coupled with the aggressive interest rate hikes by various central banks, exert pressure on the recovery of profits in the Malaysian Technology Sector.
Overall, although the Technology Sector in Malaysia is still struggling in a quagmire, the rebound signals from some companies may bring new hope to investors, and these companies need to focus more precisely on quality growth to capitalize on the high-end Technology fields.

$GENM(4715.MY)$ following its earlier sell down back towards the RM 2.10 main support levels, been able to form a solid base and broke out strong towards the RM 2.40+ major resistance levels on Friday with good volume and buying momentum here.
Seems to have formed its dip region here already and if able to hold above its RM 2.30+ immediate support levels on the daily chart, could continue to rebound further towards its RM 2.45 - RM 2.50+ major resistance until its next pullback.

$LHI(6633.MY)$ on the other hand been able to breakout towards the RM 0.63 regions with good volume and buying momentum, following the recent bird flu that hit across USA, sending egg prices soaring high up.
For now looking strong here and will be facing its RM 0.635 - RM 0.65+ major resistance levels soon. As long as able to hold above its RM 0.60 support, could breakout and trend back up towards the RM 0.66 - RM 0.69+ regions soon for an uptrend continuation pattern.

NOTION for now still have some support around RM 0.48 here and needs to hold strongly before we can expect any further rebound from this stock here.
YBS on the other hand broke past below its RM 0.53+ major support levels and retraced back towards the RM 0.47 regions earlier in the morning. Although was able to rebound back towards the RM 0.595 regions, still not looking too good yet here.

author: Lucas Cheah
body:
99SMART

Key Earnings Drivers

1. Extensive Retail Network
o 99SMART operates over 2,651 outlets across Malaysia, strategically located to cater to daily consumer needs. This widespread presence has solidified its market position and significantly contributed to its revenue stream.

Challenges
1. Market Competition
o The Malaysian retail sector is highly competitive, with numerous players vying for market share. 99SMART faces challenges in differentiating itself and maintaining customer loyalty amidst aggressive pricing and promotional strategies by competitors.

2. Operational Costs
o Expansion plans, including opening new outlets and upgrading existing ones, require substantial capital expenditure. Managing these costs while ensuring profitability is a critical challenge for 99SMART.

Growth Opportunities
1. Digital Transformation
o Investing in e-commerce platforms and digital payment solutions can enhance customer convenience and expand market reach.

2. Product Diversification
o Introducing private label products and expanding the range of offerings can attract a broader customer base and improve profit margins.

Outlook
99SMART's extensive retail footprint and consistent financial performance position it well for sustained growth. However, the company must navigate competitive pressures and manage operational costs effectively to maintain its market leadership and enhance shareholder value.

GENM

Key Earnings Drivers
1. Diversified Leisure and Hospitality Portfolio
o GENM operates a wide range of properties, including resorts, casinos, and theme parks, attracting both domestic and international tourists. This diversification has been pivotal in driving revenue growth.

Challenges
1. Regulatory Environment
o The gaming industry is subject to stringent regulations, and any changes in policies or tax structures can significantly impact GENM's operations and profitability.

2. Economic Sensitivity
o The leisure and hospitality sector is sensitive to economic fluctuations. Economic downturns or reduced consumer spending can adversely affect visitation rates and, consequently, revenue.

Growth Opportunities
1. Tourism Growth
o With the global easing of travel restrictions, there is an anticipated increase in international tourist arrivals, which could boost occupancy rates and gaming revenues.

2. Expansion Initiatives
o GENM's investments in new attractions and facilities, such as the expansion of Resorts World Genting, are expected to enhance visitor experience and drive higher footfall.s

Outlook
GENM's diversified portfolio and recent financial upturn suggest a positive outlook for future earnings. Nonetheless, the company must remain vigilant regarding regulatory changes and economic conditions to sustain its growth momentum and safeguard profitability.

In summary, both 99SMART and GENM exhibit strong foundations and growth prospects within their respective industries. Strategic management of inherent challenges and leveraging growth opportunities will be crucial for these companies to capitalize on market potential and enhance shareholder value.

title: Foreign investors sold Malaysian stocks for 0.56 billion last week.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 24th) Foreign capital continued to Sell Malaysian stocks last week with an even heavier sell-off, recording a net Sell of 0.5 billion 62 million Ringgit for the entire week, extending the net Sell trend into the 18th week.
MIDF Research pointed out through the Capital Trend report that foreign capital has been fleeing from Malaysian stocks, with the largest sell-off occurring on Monday, recording a net Sell of 0.1 billion 89.6 million Ringgit.
The three major sectors where foreign capital exited last week were Medical Care stocks (0.4 billion 44.3 million Ringgit), Utilities (0.1 billion 16 million Ringgit), and Financial Services (0.1 billion 10.4 million Ringgit).
In contrast, the sectors with the highest foreign capital inflow were Construction (73.4 million Ringgit), Consumer stocks (47.5 million Ringgit), and Telecommunications and Media (26.2 million Ringgit).
In comparison, local Institutions continued to support the Malaysian stock market, net buying 0.3 billion 16.3 million Ringgit, an increase of over four times compared to the previous week's 77.9 million Ringgit.
Retail investors continued to enter the market last week, net buying a total of 0.2 billion 45.7 million Ringgit worth of Malaysian stocks.
In terms of participation, the average daily trading volume (ADTV) increased for all parties last week, with foreign capital rising 9.7%, and local Institutions and retail investors rising by 4.7% and 11.3% respectively.

title: GENM Financial Report 27/2/2025
author: 不吃鱼
body:
I. Financial Condition Analysis
1. Revenue Performance
– Fourth Quarter (4Q2024 vs 4Q2023):
In the fourth quarter of 2024, Genting Malaysia's revenue was 2.7283 billion Ringgit, a slight increase of 0.25% (0.68 million Ringgit) compared to 2.7215 billion Ringgit in the same period of 2023. The growth was mainly driven by increased revenue from leisure and hotel operations in the United Kingdom and Egypt (16.7 million Ringgit), but was partially offset by fluctuations in the Malaysia and USA Business.
– Full Year (FY2024 vs FY2023):
Total revenue for the fiscal year 2024 was 10.9118 billion Ringgit, an increase of 0.7224 billion Ringgit (7%) compared to 10.1894 billion Ringgit in 2023. By region:
◦ Malaysia: an increase of 0.4075 billion Ringgit (6%), benefiting from the increase in business volume at Genting Highlands (RWG).
◦ United Kingdom and Egypt: an increase of 0.2282 billion Ringgit (14%), indicating strong market demand.
◦ USA and Bahamas: an increase of 0.1045 billion Ringgit (6%), mainly contributed by Resorts World New York City (RWNYC).
InterpretationThe annual revenue growth reflects the company's resilience and expansion capability in the Global market, particularly performing well in the United Kingdom and Egypt. However, growth in the Malaysian market is relatively moderate, possibly affected by local competition or economic slowdown.
2. Profitability
– Excluding the impact of exchange rates:
◦ 4Q2024: 0.1806 billion Ringgit, down 79% from 0.8439 billion Ringgit in 4Q2023. The main reason is the adjusted LBITDA (loss) of 0.4345 billion Ringgit from investments and other businesses, dragged down by an unrealized exchange loss of 0.3569 billion Ringgit.
◦ FY2024: 2.9104 billion Ringgit, an 11% increase from 2.6322 billion Ringgit in FY2023. The growth comes from increased revenue but is partially offset by rising operational costs.
– Excluding the impact of exchange rates:
◦ The adjusted EBITDA for FY2024 is 2.795 billion Ringgit, slightly down from 2.8033 billion Ringgit in FY2023 (<1%), indicating that the core Business profitability remains basically stable.
– Pre-tax profit:
FY2024 is 0.4867 billion Ringgit, a 28% decrease from FY2023's 0.6742 billion Ringgit, mainly affected by asset write-offs (0.2165 billion Ringgit), increased financing costs (55 million Ringgit), and lower asset disposal gains.
InterpretationAlthough EBITDA grew for the year, profitability in the fourth quarter declined significantly due to exchange losses. Core Business performance remained steady, but non-recurring factors (such as exchange rate fluctuations and asset impairments) put pressure on overall profits.
3. Costs and Expenses
– Operating Costs: Operating expenses and labor costs generally increased in 2024, particularly in the Malaysian, United Kingdom, and USA markets, putting pressure on profit margins.
– Asset Impairment and Write-offs:
The scrap amount of property, factory, and equipment for FY2024 surged to 0.2165 billion Ringgit (compared to 17.5 million Ringgit in FY2023).
The impairment loss was 35.08 million Ringgit, a slight increase from 33.31 million Ringgit in FY2023.
InterpretationThe increase in costs and asset scrapping reflects the company's investment in expansion or asset renewal but also exposes deficiencies in cost control and asset return efficiency.
4. Financial Health
– Cash Flow:
The net cash flow from operating activities for FY2024 was 2.475 billion Ringgit, a slight decrease from 2.5814 billion Ringgit in FY2023.
Net outflow from investing activities was 1.2631 billion Ringgit for property and equipment purchases; net outflow from financing activities was 1.2438 billion Ringgit for debt repayment and dividends.
– Debt:
◦ As of December 31, 2024, total borrowings are 12.2208 billion Ringgit, essentially flat compared to 12.2166 billion Ringgit in 2023.
◦ Long-term borrowings account for 97.7%, indicating a stable debt structure.
InterpretationCash flow has slightly declined, but is sufficient to support Operation and investment needs. The debt level is manageable, but attention is needed on future interest burdens and exchange rate risks related to US dollar debt.
5. Segment Performance
– Malaysia: Revenue increased by 6%, but EBITDA margin dropped from 29% to 28%, revealing cost pressures.
– United Kingdom and Egypt: Revenue grew by 14%, EBITDA declined by 39%, and operational efficiency needs improvement.
– USA and the Bahamas: Revenue grew by 6%, EBITDA decreased by 42%, and labor costs significantly increased.
Interpretation: Revenue growth in various segments has not effectively converted into profits, highlighting challenges in Operation efficiency and cost management.
II. Current Situation
Genting Malaysia's performance in 2024 shows a dual aspect:
1. Positive Factors:
◦ Stable revenue growth (7%), demonstrating the company's competitiveness in the Global Gambling and hotel market.
◦ Healthy Cash flow and debt structure support ongoing Operation and expansion.
The United Kingdom and USA markets still have growth potential, especially with potential opportunities from new casino licenses in New York.
2. Negative Factors:
The profitability is affected by exchange loss (0.3569 billion Ringgit) and asset write-offs (0.2165 billion Ringgit).
Rising costs are eroding profit margins, and operational efficiency needs to be optimized.
In the fourth quarter, there was a pre-tax loss of 0.3682 billion Ringgit, reflecting short-term financial pressure.
SummaryThe company's fundamentals are solid, but short-term impact from non-core factors is significant, and internal optimization is needed to relieve pressure.
Three, Future Outlook
1. Macroeconomic Environment
– Global Economy: Geopolitical tensions and trade frictions may hinder economic growth, affecting tourism and Gambling demand.
– Malaysia: Domestic demand supports economic growth, but inflation and policy adjustments bring uncertainty.
– International Tourism: The global travel recovery trend is Bullish for the regional Gambling market.
2. Company Strategy and Opportunities
– Malaysia:
◦ Optimize marketing strategy to increase visitor numbers at Genting Highlands.
◦ Infrastructure upgrades and new attractions (such as eco-tourism projects) and the 60th-anniversary celebration activities are expected to stimulate demand.
– United Kingdom:
◦ Focus on operational efficiency and cost control, launching innovative products to enhance competitiveness.
– USA:
◦ Strategic expansion (such as RWNYC and Empire synergy) and the application for a new casino license in New York are key growth points.
◦ Collaborating with international cruise lines to enhance business in the Bahamas.
3. Risk Factors
– Exchange rate risk: A high proportion of debts in USD means that fluctuations in Exchange Rates may continue to affect profits.
– Legal litigation: The $0.6 billion lawsuit faced by the USA subsidiary may pose financial and reputational risks.
– Market Competition: Competition in the Gambling and hotel Industry is intensifying, and market share must be maintained.
OutlookIn the short term, the company needs to cope with cost and exchange rate pressures, remaining cautiously optimistic; in the long term, if efficiency can be optimized and opportunities in the USA market captured, growth potential is considerable.
4. Investment Advice
The valuation and prospects of Genting Malaysia need to be considered comprehensively:
– Advantages.The Global business layout is stable, cash flow is sufficient, and the potential in the USA market is significant.
– Hidden worries.Short-term profit fluctuations are large, requiring strengthened cost control and risk management.
– RecommendationCurrently, it is recommendedWait and see., to closely monitor the company's cost optimization measures, the progress of the New York license, and the effectiveness of exchange rate risk management.

author: 风起云涌LBF
body: In total for the year, Genting Malaysia ~GENM, 4715 netted 0.2 billion 51.28 million Ringgit, a decline of 42.27% year-on-year, while revenue increased by 7.09% year-on-year, reaching 10.9 billion 11.82 million Ringgit. Additionally, Genting Malaysia announced a final dividend of 4 cents per share, with the ex-dividend date on March 14, and payment to be made on April 10. Genting Malaysia pointed out that its loans settled in US dollars incurred an unrealized forex conversion loss of 0.3 billion 56.9 million Ringgit in the last quarter due to unfavorable forex conditions. Excluding the impact of forex, the company's adjusted EBITDA decreased by 25% year-on-year in the last quarter. Looking ahead, Genting Malaysia is cautiously optimistic about the short-term prospects of the Leisure tourism Industry, and indicates that the long-term outlook in related fields remains positive. For the year as a whole, Genting ~ GENTING, 3182 accumulated a net profit of 0.8 billion 82.95 million Ringgit, a year-on-year decline of 4.98%, while revenue slightly increased by 2.21% year-on-year, to 27.7 billion 17.02 million Ringgit. In addition, Genting announced a final dividend of 5 cents per share, with an ex-dividend date of March 14, and to be distributed on April 16. Genting pointed out that its Resorts World Sentosa (RWS), Resorts World Genting (RWG), Resorts World New York City (RWNYC), and Resorts World Bimini all showed a decrease in revenue in the last quarter. At the same time, the strengthening of the Ringgit against the British Pound, US Dollar, and Singapore Dollar has also led to a decrease in the company's revenue and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA). Genting announced several personnel changes, including Tan Sri Lim Kok Thay stepping down as Chief Executive Officer after nearly 20 years, transitioning to Executive Chairman, while President, Chief Operating Officer, and Executive Director Dato' Sri Chian Kwang Han will become Chief Executive Officer, effective March 1. Meanwhile, Chian Kwang Han will also step down from his position as Chief Executive Officer of Genting Plantations (GENP, 2291, Main Board Plantations), to be succeeded by Lim Kok Thay's eldest son, Dato' Indra Lim Kong Hui, who will also take effect from March 1.

title: Poor performance has faced selling pressure, and the Market Cap of the Genting duo has evaporated by over 3.3 billion.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
The quarterly performance turned red, and the key figure, Tan Sri Lim Kok Thay, has left the management team. $GENTING (3182.MY)$ Genting and $GENM (4715.MY)$ Genting Malaysia's stock price suffered a double blow today, with the Market Cap of the duo evaporating by more than 3.3 billion Ringgit overnight!
Genting (GENTING) saw a drop of nearly 12%, while Genting Malaysia (GENM) experienced a more severe decline, plunging by as much as 16%.
Due to adverse Forex conditions and the weakening of Leisure and Entertainment business, Genting and Genting Malaysia both turned from profit to loss by the end of the 2024 fiscal year (as of December), with net losses of 0.1 billion Ringgit and 0.4 billion Ringgit respectively.
At the same time, Genting also announced several personnel changes, including Tan Sri Lim Kok Thay stepping down as CEO after nearly 20 years in the position to become Executive Chairman.
Meanwhile, President, COO, and Executive Director Dato' Sri Chen Guanghan will assume the role of CEO, effective from March 1.
Chen Guanghan will also step down from the position of CEO of Genting Plantations. $GENP (2291.MY)$ The CEO position will be taken over by the current Deputy CEO Dato' Indra Lin Konghui, also effective from March 1.
Lin Gonghui is the eldest son of Lin Guotai.

title: Publishing Earnings Reports after trading hours is extremely unfavorable for retail investors, as Institutions and executives may have already adjusted their
author: QQ_
body:
Publishing Earnings Reports after trading hours is extremely unfavorable for retail investors, as Institutions and executives may have already adjusted their Hold Positions in advance, leaving retail investors to passively endure market fluctuations.

Regulatory bodies should establish fairer rules, such as mandating Earnings Reports to be released during trading hours, monitoring insider trading behavior, and improving market transparency.

Retail investors should manage risks before the Earnings Reports to avoid being affected by market volatility; long-term investors can pay attention to dividends and fundamentals, adhering to a long-term strategy. There is serious suspicion of intentional exploitation, the executives are excessively indulgent.

author: QQ_
body:
In Q4, there was a loss of -457.90 million MYR, but this was mainly due to one-time asset impairment and Forex losses, not a business issue; the market has overreacted.

Reasonable valuation:
NTA = 2.10 - 2.25 MYR, with the current stock price at 1.90 MYR, it is already below asset value.
Short-term Target Price = 2.50 - 3.00 MYR (after Q1 performance recovery).
Long-term reasonable price = 3.50 - 5.00 MYR (profit continuing to recover).

Strategy:
1. Continue to increase positions at 1.80 - 1.70 MYR to lower costs.
2. Sell part at 2.50 - 3.00 MYR to lock in profits.
3. Hold for the long term and wait for the market to recover, challenging above 3.50 MYR.
Market sentiment fluctuates in the short term, GENM will certainly return to reasonable value in the future!

title: For 19 consecutive weeks, there has been a major outflow as foreign investors aggressively sold Malaysian stocks last week, totaling 1.27 billion.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 3rd) Foreign funds continued to sell Malaysian stocks last week, with an even heavier selling intensity, recording a net sell of 1.2 billion 70 million Ringgit for the week, maintaining the net selling trend for the 19th week.
MIDF Research pointed out through the Capital Trend report that foreign funds continuously fled Malaysian stocks last week, with the heaviest selling occurring on Friday, recording a net sell of 0.6 billion 46.2 million Ringgit.
The three major sectors that saw foreign outflow last week were financial services (-0.3 billion 62.1 million Ringgit), consumer and services (-0.3 billion 14.9 million Ringgit), and utilities (-0.2 billion 55.1 million Ringgit).
In contrast, the sectors with the most foreign purchases were construction (24.1 million Ringgit), telecommunications and media (14.7 million Ringgit), and REITs (6.7 million Ringgit).
In comparison, local Institutions remained the backbone of Malaysian stocks, with a net buy of 0.8 billion 17.4 million Ringgit.
Retail investors continued to enter last week, with a total net buy of 0.4 billion 47.9 million Ringgit of Malaysian stocks.
In terms of participation, the average daily trading volume (ADTV) fluctuated significantly last week, with foreign capital increasing by 80.3%, local Institutions rising by 5.8%; retail investors declined by 1.6%.
