title: Bursa Q4 Earnings Summary And Reflection
author: Ultraboom
body:
Bursa just wrapped up its earnings season, >1000 companies have reported their earnings, and this might be the worst QR season I've experienced since I started investing in 2023, many companies experienced >10% with some even >30% dump since start of 2025. Those that reported good earnings didnt even see any bump, but rather get to keep their current price level. Bursa is currrently in a bear market, defensive picks tend to do well, as we can see below
Winners :
1. Plantation : I would say the biggest winners this season is plantation, most reported record QR, some even on track for record year, most paid dividend, some even special dividends. But most didnt see any share price rally, but in a bear market where everything is crashing, not getting dumped is a good thing, with a nice dividend as a reward for holding. Moving forward, as long as CPO price can maintain at current level, baring any external factors, i expect them to do well for the rest of 2025. (PS - my current largest holding is a plantation stock).
2. Banks : This is no surprise as banks tend to do well as long as country economy is doing well, msia GDP growth for Q4 2024 was 5%, down from 5.4% in Q3 but full year gdp growth was 5.1% which is much improved from 3.6% in 2023. Lesson for retailers reading this, banks are proxy to a countries economy, most malaysian banks are conventional banks aka 'farmers', they tend to do so so, tracking gdp growth of a country, this contrast investment banks or IBs, which is more 'hunter' business, their performance tend to track stock market performance. I tend to avoid investing in msian banks cos I'm looking for higher returns, and i dont see banks delivering 15-20% yoy growth on earnings, but i did have a good call on $ABMB (2488.MY)$ in 2023, the thesis was they are the bank with the highest ROE while having lowest PBV, and their value was realised when All eyes on Vertical Theme’s next move in Alliance Bank
3. Reits : Same as banks, reits tend to do so so, as property is a stable business, im also not a fan of reits, for the same reason as banks, the return isnt high enough to justify the effort and risk im taking. I did owned $PAVREIT (5212.MY)$ in 2023 when i started investing, it was a good call as at that time market 'forgot' that they injected pavillion bukit jalil into the trust but the value wasnt reflected back then
Losers
1. Technology : By far the biggest loser is technology, esp OSAT and ATE players, with only a few exceptions like $FRONTKN (0128.MY)$ maybe $KGB (0151.MY)$ if u consider KGB as a 'semicon' counter, the other OSAT and ATE players are facing double whammy of reducing sales and compressed margins, mainly from competition from china players, which are competing for both orders and at a cheaper price, this is a very grim outlook. On top of all that, the OSAT players need to spend capex on advance packaging as not to be left behind. Decreasing revenue, compressed margins and need for more capex, i personally do not have any ATE or OSAT counters as i view them as almost the start of sunset industry, similar to what happened to gloves after covid. The only way out for them is to spend capex to upgrade themselves, but whether they can spend capex to catch up before they run out of money is the big question, the only promising one is $VITROX (0097.MY)$ hence they got to keep their relatively higher valuation vs peers, but do they deserve that high valuation given they are going to spend capex and will face compressed margins? only time will tell. I'm glad that i cut loss on $TTVHB (0272.MY)$ earlier, as the stock is down another 50% from my exit price, guess my call was right.
2. Oil And Gas : Another badly hit sector, most O&G counters in bursa are petronas capex contractors, hence relying on petronas contracts, their performance tend to track petronas capex cycle, given petronas recent 'rightsizing'(should just call it downsizing), the sentiment has been poor, even while most report decent earnings, some like $ARMADA (5210.MY)$ $VELESTO (5243.MY)$ $WASCO (5142.MY)$ even resume paying dividends after years of hiatus, but seems like market isnt buying it, the outliers seems to be $DELEUM (5132.MY)$ , which is no surprise as they are petronas opex. Along with $HAWK (0320.MY)$ , they tend to be more stable and defensive, wont experience boom during upcycle but wont make losses during downturn
3. Consumers : This was a surprise for me, while the earnings were decent, i personally think this is more of a sentiment thing, a result foreigners selling, this is backed by fundflow data. Consumers tend to be more defensive, you'd expect them to do well even in downturns like now, but as usual, sentiment can affect their valuation, especially for large caps like $MRDIY (5296.MY)$ $99SMART (5326.MY)$, both experience some sort of dump, worst hit was definitely $GENTING (3182.MY)$ $GENM (4715.MY)$, while breweries like $CARLSBG (2836.MY)$ $HEIM (3255.MY)$ did okay, helped by their dividends
Conclusion
Theres a saying that the stock market testing ground both investors and companies, it test companies ability to deliver earnings growth, while it test investors abiity to find and hold good companies. These are trying times, where the men get separated from the boys, wheat gets separated from the chaff so to speak. How and what you do as investor during these times will determine your success or failure.
Overall, out of my 7 holdings, 6/7 have reported earnings, only 1/7 was below expectation, and dumped 30% from the peak, but due to my emphasis on margin of safety, yours truly is only down 10% on that stock. 4/7 declared dividends, one resumption after 10 years, two had record earnings and dividend. I'm expecting 1 more QR at end march, which hopefully will be record earnings as well.
My portfolio is down from the peak in Dec 2024, i expect most people to be no different, in fact its down 9%+ YTD, but still overall in the green when accounted for past capital gains and dividends. As mentioned in previous post, strategy for 2025 is to hold more cash and average in as i see fit. So far, i would like to see more weakenss before i deploy capital, but i also know you cant time the bottom
As usual, none of what i said should be considered as financial advice, always do your own research, any question, feel free to comment below, these are hard times, we need all the support we can get.

title: Why Are Foreigners Dumping Malaysian Banks While Locals Gobble Up CIMB？
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Hey everyone!
Another wild week in markets as Trump's tariffs send shockwaves across the globe.
Foreign investors have been selling off for 20 consecutive weeks, and the capital outflow since the start of this year has already surpassed the total for 2024.
Let's take an in-depth look at the capital flows of last week and witness the divergence among investors on bank stocks.
Market Pulse: Tariffs, Jobs, and Central Banks
What’s Shaking:
US factories barely clung to growth (ISM: 50.3) as prices for raw materials shot up. Meanwhile, job growth disappointed, only 151k new roles added, way below expectations.
The Fed kept rates on hold but warned Trump’s tariffs could spark inflation. The ECB cut rates to 2.65% as Europe’s economy sputters.
China tried to juice spending with a $41.7 billion stimulus, but prices still fell 0.7% YoY.
Market Reactions:
Last week US tech stocks tanked (Nasdaq -3.45%), while Indonesia (+5.83%) and Hong Kong (+5.62%) rallied on hopes of more stimulus. As we all know, on Monday, US stocks experienced their biggest tech-related decline since 2022.
Oil dropped to $70.36/bbl, and the Ringgit strengthened to RM4.4120 against the dollar.
Asia’s Money Moves: Foreigners Flee, Philippines Scores
The Big Picture:
Foreign investors yanked out a massive $8.17 billion from Asian markets for the second week straight. Only the Philippines (+$6.94 billion) saw inflows, thanks to stable US defense ties.
Hotspots:
Taiwan: Lost $4.76 billion as $Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM.US)$'s $100 billion US expansion spooked investors.
India: 13th week of outflows (-$2.83 billion) amid fears of US steel tariffs.
South Korea: 8th week of selling (-$187 million) despite green bond launches.
Malaysia Market Breakdown: Foreigners Flee Financials, Locals Defend
Foreigners Hit the Panic Button:
Dumped RM881.5 million for the 20th week in a row, with banks (-RM407 million) and consumer stocks (-RM215 million) taking the worst hits.
But they did dip into tech (RM40 million) and telecom (RM26 million).
Locals Step Up:
Institutions poured RM617 million into banks ($CIMB (1023.MY)$ RM336 million) and energy ( $TENAGA (5347.MY)$ RM113 million).
Retail investors piled into CIMB (RM97 million) and $GENM (4715.MY)$ (RM80 million), but trimmed holdings in weaker banks like $PBBANK (1295.MY)$ (-RM49 million).
Stock Spotlight: Who’s Buying What?
Foreigners:
They're spooked by global trade chaos and US rate hikes. They're ditching banks and hiding in healthcare ($KPJ (5878.MY)$).
Institutions:
Betting on Malaysia's domestic strength. They’re doubling down on banks ($CIMB (1023.MY)$) and energy ($TENAGA (5347.MY)$) for steady dividends.
$PBBANK (1295.MY)$ $RHBBANK (1066.MY)$ $NATGATE (0270.MY)$ $IHH (5225.MY)$
Bottom Line: Foreigners are playing defense, locals are playing offense.
Wildcard: $MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ saw a massive RM427 million in block trades.
Risks to Watch
1) Tariffs could escalate further.
2) The Fed might hike rates if inflation spikes.
3) Global growth could slow faster than expected.
This is the first time we've observed the flow of funds. Got questions? Drop them below!

I pivoted away from Malaysian stocks in favour of participating in the more liquid, volatile (in a good way), and more dynamic US stocks market.

title: Continuous 21 weeks of large-scale selling, foreign investors net sold Malaysian stocks worth 1.34 billion last week.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
The selling pressure from foreign investment on Malaysian stocks has not yet reached its end, with a net selling amount of 1.34 billion Ringgit last week, and the net outflow trend has continued for 21 weeks so far.
MIDF Research pointed out in its Capital Trend report that foreign investors have been continuously net selling Malaysian stocks last week, with the largest selling occurring on Tuesday, recording a net selling amount of 0.46 billion Ringgit.
The three sectors where foreign investors exited the most last week were financial services (-0.73 billion Ringgit), consumer and services (-0.12 billion Ringgit), and utilities (-0.19 billion Ringgit).
In contrast, the sectors where foreign investors bought the most were construction (0.18 billion Ringgit), Technology (22 million Ringgit), and Energy (6.4 million Ringgit).
In comparison, local Institutions remain the mainstay of Malaysian stocks, maintaining their position of net buying Malaysian stocks for the 21st week, recording a net buying amount of 1.10 billion Ringgit for the entire week.
Retail investors continued to enter the market for the fifth week, with a total net buying of 31.5 million Ringgit, lower than the previous week's 0.64 billion Ringgit.
In terms of participation, the average daily trading volume (ADTV) for foreign investors and local Institutions increased by 11.0% and 10.9% respectively, while retail investors decreased by 1.6%.
The report shows that despite significant selling of bank stocks by foreign investors, they still bought into certain stocks. $RHBBANK (1066.MY)$ 。
Foreign capital is heavily selling off stocks.

title: CreditSights: The credit outlook for Genting's dual giants is good this year, but bad next year.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 20th) Fitch's CreditSights, a credit market research institution, believes that the demand in the Gambling, Leisure, and Hotel Industry remains robust, thus, Genting $GENTING (3182.MY)$ and Resorts World Genting Malaysia $GENM (4715.MY)$ The crediting outlook is expected to gradually improve this year.
However, the Institutions also stated that the crediting outlook for Genting Group will worsen next year, mainly due to accelerated investments.
CreditSights analysts noted in a report that supported by strong demand in the gambling, leisure, and hospitality industry, the crediting outlook for Genting and Genting Malaysia is expected to gradually improve by fiscal year 2025 (ending December).
The analysts also predict that the revenue and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) for Genting and Genting Malaysia will increase by 3% to 7% this year.
In terms of capital expenditure, analysts estimate that Genting will only slightly increase investment this year, but next year, influenced by the expansion plans of Resorts World Sentosa (RWS) and Resorts World New York, investments will accelerate.
We expect Genting's free cash flow to come under pressure and turn negative in fiscal year 2026.
Therefore, while the outlook is optimistic this year, the analysts believe that the crediting outlook for Genting and Genting Malaysia may deteriorate next year.
The capital expenditure for Resorts World New York is expected to be substantial, Genting may primarily finance through debt, and the negative impacts brought by this may overshadow the bullish EBITDA profit growth.
Overall, CreditSights has started to track Genting and Genting Malaysia, giving ratings of "Market Perform" and "Outperform" respectively.

author: Zamm
body:
Comparing Malaysia's tourism industry to that of Macau reveals some differences. Macau's tourism sector has been heavily reliant on gambling, which has faced challenges in recent years. The Macau government has recognized the need for economic diversification and has introduced the "1+4" development strategy to reduce reliance on gambling by promoting industries such as life sciences, financial technology, advanced technology, and large-scale event production. Despite these efforts, Macau continues to face challenges in achieving sustainable growth, partly due to its limited land and human resources.

In contrast, Malaysia's tourism industry is more diversified, encompassing eco-tourism, cultural tourism, medical tourism, and more. This diversification, coupled with ongoing efforts to enhance sustainability and align with ESG principles, positions Malaysia's tourism sector for continued growth leading up to and beyond Visit Malaysia Year 2026.

title: Time, place, and harmony among people.
author: 风起云涌LBF
body:
Once during class, the teacher asked us a question:

"Can hard work really change fate?"

Most students, including me, believe that hard work can change fate.

The teacher smiled and posed another question:

If you were born in a poor and backward country or in a country plagued by war for many years, do you think that with your innate intelligence and effort, you could also escape that kind of environment?

Everyone fell silent. Although reluctant to accept that "efforts may not necessarily change fate," this is a very realistic fact.

It doesn't mean we shouldn't strive; effort is essential. I believe the teacher's intended meaning is:

Do not attribute all of your beautiful (or successful) life solely to your efforts and feel complacent.

The success of an endeavor depends on many factors.

Otherwise, why would there be sayings like 'the right time, the right place, and the right people'? That is the meaning.
While working hard, a lot of luck, benefactors, and so on are also needed.

One should have a grateful heart, appreciating one's genes and everything encountered.

If one has enough ability, then help those who start at a disadvantage from birth.

#Ovarian Lottery

Everyone fell silent. Although reluctant to accept that "efforts may not necessarily change fate," this is a very realistic fact.
It doesn't mean we shouldn't strive; effort is essential. I believe the teacher's intended meaning is:
Do not attribute all of your beautiful (or successful) life solely to your efforts and feel complacent.
The success of an endeavor depends on many factors.
Otherwise, why would there be sayings like 'the right time, the right place, and the right people'? That is the meaning.
While working hard, a lot of luck, benefactors, and so on are also needed.
One should have a grateful heart, appreciating one's genes and everything encountered.
If one has enough ability, then help those who start at a disadvantage from birth.

title: When I first started working, I heard some old seniors say that buying Genting was a good investment, with dividends every year. Just look at how many people
body: When I first started working, I heard some old seniors say that buying Genting was a good investment, with dividends every year. Just look at how many people go there to gamble, bringing money, it's an indispensable vacation spot for holidays and trips, and the hotels are always full. So many people go there every day. When Mr. Lim built the amusement park on the mountain, many people said he was foolish, so far away, so high, but now it has turned into a city that never sleeps. Every time I went there, I would pack KFC + curry chicken + bread. Once we checked into the hotel, we would eat a couple of pieces of bread and curry chicken before heading out to play: old cars, boating, the thrill ride, and a bucket of 20 cent arcade games. In the evening, we would go to Yunhua Palace to watch performances, where tigers could disappear. Late at night, while my parents were gambling, we kids would sneak KFC. The next day, if my parents won money, we would have dim sum; if they lost, we would eat dry noodles at the taxi station. Now that we have grown up, we understand investment, perhaps like Mr. Li, we only believe in it.

title: A net outflow for 23 consecutive weeks, foreign investors sold Malaysian stocks worth 1.15 billion last week.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
The trend of foreign capital net selling Malaysian stocks has continued into the 23rd week, although the net selling has slowed down, the total amount still reached 1.15 billion Ringgit.
MIDF Research reported today through its Capital Trend report that foreign capital was selling Malaysian stocks last week, with the heaviest selling pressure occurring on Friday, recording a net selling amount of 0.3 billion 84 million Ringgit.
The sectors that experienced the highest net selling by foreign capital last week were financial services (-0.5 billion 64.4 million Ringgit), Consumer and Services (-0.1 billion 42.3 million Ringgit), and Medical Care (-0.1 billion 18.1 million Ringgit).
At the same time, foreign capital only net bought in two sectors last week, which were construction (7.1 million Ringgit) and plantation (3.9 million Ringgit).
Local institutions remain the largest buyers of Malaysian stocks, maintaining their net buying for the 23rd week, recording a net buying amount of 1.2 billion 40 million Ringgit throughout the week.
Local retail investors reversed the previous six weeks' net buying trend, net selling Malaysian stocks of 87.9 million Ringgit last week.
In terms of participation, all three parties saw a decline, with foreign capital’s average daily trading volume (ADTV) experiencing the largest drop of 34.7%, while local institutions and retail investors fell by 12.7% and 13.8% respectively.

title: Missing someone is a kind of illness.
body:
When you are on the other side of crossing mountains and ridges 📉
I am on a lonely road with no end 📈
How much in a lifetime is too late.
Realizing that the most important thing has already been lost.
Suddenly realizing that it has long since faded away.
Why is it only after making mistakes that one is willing to believe the fault lies with oneself.
They say this is life, trying to understand.
Trying to hold back tears, but still unable to escape the emotions that should be felt.
I won't demand that the world stop turning.
I know that escaping is completely useless.
It's just during this time, especially at night.

Everyone goes through a learning process, and learning financial literacy is very important. I am just an ordinary worker who only knew how to earn money through labor for 18 years. It was only after the pandemic that I began to slowly engage and understand, seeking legitimate channels for learning (during the process, there were instances of being deceived due to greed and insufficient awareness...).
Choosing friends is very important.
Fortunately, I now have a good teacher. My teacher never makes recommendations or diagnoses, nor does he want us to listen to rumors. He wants each of us to become independent, learn to read charts, study techniques, and most importantly, have the right mindset.
The journey is still long... Let's keep going, fellow stock enthusiasts.

body:
A total of 36 warrants will be expiring within the next few weeks. These include warrants over Malaysian stocks such as MY E.G. Services (MYEG), 99 Speed Mart (99SMART) and Tenaga Nasional (TENAGA) amongst others. Other warrants expiring soon include warrants over the Hang Seng Index (HSI), which still see active trading as of today, and Hong Kong stocks from the likes of Xiaomi Corporation (XIAOMI), Alibaba Group (ALIBABA) and others. Investors should note that all structured warrants listed on Bursa Malaysia must stop trading 1 business day before their expiry date. This means the last day a warrant can be traded, i.e., the last trading date (LTD) will be the second business day before its expiry date. For instance, HSI-CWCN, which still sees trading activity today, will be expiring on 29th April – the LTD for this warrant alongside the other HSI warrants expiring in April will be on 25th April, meaning investors will no longer be able to buy or sell these warrants after the LTD. title: Will there be a stock market crash in the next two years.
author: 旋风小肥侠
body:
The risk of a significant stock market crash occurring in the next two years is notably present, but it is not inevitable. The key factors depend on:
- Whether the valuation of the US stock market can be digested through earnings growth;
- Whether the Federal Reserve's policies can timely respond to the economic slowdown;
- Whether geopolitical conflicts escalate into a systemic crisis.

2. **Investor strategy**
- **Defensive allocation**: Focus on companies with low debt and stable cash flow, or long-term growth areas such as the GREEN ECONOMY.
- **Diversify risk**: Increase non-US Assets (such as Emerging Markets, CSI Commodity Equity Index) to hedge against US stock volatility.
- **Avoid excessive leverage**: History shows that high leverage is a major cause of amplified losses during crashes.

In summary, the market may experience severe fluctuations or even phased crashes in the next two years, but whether a comprehensive major stock market crash occurs will depend on policy responses and Global economic resilience. Investors need to remain cautious of risks while avoiding overreactions and maintaining a long-term perspective.

China said Friday that it's "currently evaluating" the "multiple messages" that Washington has sent Beijing about opening trade talks aimed to easing the two nations' ongoing trade-and-tariff war.
Bloomberg News reported Friday that China has quietly lifted import duties on about a quarter of the American items originally impacted.

title: While the full acquisition of Empire Resorts (and therefore 100% ownership of Resorts World Catskills and Resorts World Hudson Valley) by Genting Malaysia Bhd
author: Tranquility
body: While the full acquisition of Empire Resorts (and therefore 100% ownership of Resorts World Catskills and Resorts World Hudson Valley) by Genting Malaysia Bhd could be a positive factor in their bid for a full casino license in New York, it's not the sole determining factor and doesn't guarantee success. Here's why it could be helpful and other factors at play: Potential Benefits of Full Ownership for License Application: * Simplified Operations and Decision-Making: Full ownership allows Genting Malaysia to streamline the management and strategic direction of all its New York properties. This could present a more cohesive and integrated vision to the New York State Gaming Commission regarding their plans for a full-scale casino. * Enhanced Financial Control: With 100% ownership, Genting Malaysia has complete control over the financial resources and future investments in the Empire Resorts properties. This could demonstrate a stronger commitment and financial capacity to develop and operate a full casino. * Brand Consistency and Cross-Marketing: Owning all the Resorts World properties in New York outright allows for more effective branding and cross-marketing efforts between Resorts World New York City, Resorts World Catskills, and Resorts World Hudson Valley. This unified brand presence could be seen favorably by the regulators. * Long-Term Commitment Signal: The move to acquire the remaining stake could be interpreted as a strong signal of Genting Malaysia's long-term commitment to the New York gaming market. This willingness to invest further, even in a loss-making entity, might be viewed positively by the licensing authorities. * Synergies and Efficiencies: Genting Malaysia has mentioned the potential for enhanced operational synergies. Demonstrating a clear plan to leverage these synergies under full ownership to create a successful full-scale casino could strengthen their application. However, other crucial factors will heavily influence the New York State Gaming Commission's decision on awarding a full casino license by the end of 2025. These include: * Financial Stability and Track Record: While full ownership provides more control, the financial performance of Empire Resorts will still be a key consideration. The Gaming Commission will assess Genting Malaysia's overall financial health and their ability to successfully operate a large-scale casino, especially given Empire's history of losses. * Suitability and Experience: Genting Malaysia has a long track record in the gaming industry globally, including their existing operations at Resorts World New York City. This experience is a significant advantage. This includes the scale of investment, amenities, job creation, and the overall economic benefits to the region. * Community Support: Demonstrating local community support for their casino project is a vital aspect of the application process in New York. Any opposition could hinder their chances. * Competition: The competition for the limited number of full casino licenses in downstate New York is fierce. Other major gaming operators are also vying for these licenses, and their proposals will be evaluated rigorously. * Regulatory Requirements: Genting Malaysia must meet all the stringent regulatory requirements set forth by the New York State Gaming Commission, including detailed application submissions, environmental reviews, and adherence to zoning laws. * Political and Economic Landscape: The overall political and economic climate in New York could also indirectly influence the decision-making process. In conclusion, while gaining full ownership of Empire Resorts could offer Genting Malaysia several operational and strategic advantages that might strengthen their application for a full casino license, it is not a guarantee of success. The New York State Gaming Commission will conduct a comprehensive evaluation based on numerous factors, and Genting Malaysia will need a compelling proposal that addresses all the criteria to secure a license by the end of 2025.

title: Genting Malaysia's gaining full membership of Empire Resorts draws negative vibes
author: Zaclim
body:
Genting Malaysia Bhd (GenM) is back in the spotlight, and not necessarily for a good reason. The casino operator is facing scrutiny over another related party transaction (RPT) to increase its stake in Nasdaq-listed Empire Resorts Inc.
Remember the last time this happened? Back in 2019, GenM's market cap took a RM2.6 billion hit after buying a stake in Empire from its controlling shareholder. Investors weren't thrilled, and it seems like they're wary again.
Here's what's going on:
- Proposed Purchase: GenM is proposing to purchase the remaining 51% membership interest in Genting Empire Resorts LLC.
- Analyst maintains a “sell” call on the counter.
What are the negatives of doing the deal?
- Pricey and Dilutive: The purchase is seen as pricey and is expected to be profit-dilutive.
- High Valuation: The transaction implies a financial year ended Dec 31, 2024 enterprise value/earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation multiple of 72.7 times which is above trading multiples of comparable listed US peers
What are the benefits of doing the deal?
- Cohesive Brand Positioning: Allow for more cohesive brand positioning under the Resorts World umbrella.
- Operational Synergies: The consolidation is expected to unlock operational synergies, ultimately driving revenue growth and improving overall returns across both assets.
Although there is a positive investor buying in this acquisition, it will be challenging for the counter to trend higher given the negative factors surrounding the stake increase.
What do you think? Is GenM making a smart move with this deal, or is it a gamble that could backfire? #GentingMalaysia #Stocks #Investment #Malaysia #EmpireResorts

title: Malaysia Morning Wrap | BNM Cuts SRR, Holds OPR; Genting Malaysia's US$41 Million Empire Resorts Buyout Under Bursa Malaysia Scrutiny
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Good morning mooers! Here are things you need to know about today's market:
U.S. Markets Rally on UK Trade Deal.
KLCI Dips on Profit-Taking.
BNM Cuts SRR from 2% to 1%, Lowest in 14 Years, Injecting RM19 billion; OPR Held at 3%.
Malaysia-US Trade Talks: 10% Global Tariff Stays, Focus on Reciprocal Tariffs.
Stocks to watch: GENM, PBBANK, etc.
- Moomoo News MY
Wall Street Summary
$S&P 500 Index (.SPX.US)$ 5,663.94 (+0.58%)
$Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI.US)$ 41,368.45 (+0.62%)
$Nasdaq Composite Index (.IXIC.US)$ 17,928.14(+1.07%)
U.S. stock markets surged on Thursday, with the Nasdaq Composite, S&P 500, and Dow Jones all posting gains following the announcement of a bilateral trade agreement between the U.S. and UK.
This deal, which maintains the 10% minimum tariff on most imports without additional increases, sparked investor optimism for potential resolutions in ongoing trade disputes. President Trump's announcement of the UK agreement and expectations for productive talks with China over the weekend boosted market sentiment.
The positive trade outlook also influenced cryptocurrency markets, with Bitcoin briefly surpassing $100,000 for the first time since February.
Bursa Market Insight
$FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ 1542.740 (-0.46%)
Top Gainer: $YTL (4677.MY)$ RM2.11 (+2.93%)
Top Loser: $IOICORP (1961.MY)$ RM3.58 (-3.50%)
USD/MYR: $USD/MYR (USDMYR.FX)$ 4.2810(+0.00%)
The FBM KLCI closed lower on Thursday, dropping 0.46% to 1,542.74 points, as profit-taking overshadowed bargain-hunting efforts. Despite the index's decline, overall market sentiment remained positive with more gainers than losers. Trading volume increased to 3.36 billion shares worth RM2.72 billion.
Analysts anticipate cautious trading to continue on Bursa Malaysia in the near term, as investors balance profit-taking with potential buying opportunities.
Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) announced a significant reduction in the statutory reserve requirement ratio (SRR) from 2% to 1%, effective May 16, marking its lowest level in 14 years.
This move is expected to inject approximately RM19 billion of liquidity into the banking system, aimed at facilitating better liquidity management for banks amidst increased financial market volatility.
BNM clarified that the SRR adjustment is not indicative of its monetary policy stance, which is solely reflected by the overnight policy rate (OPR). Notably, the Monetary Policy Committee maintained the OPR at 3%, where it has remained since May 2023.
In ongoing Malaysia-US trade negotiations, the 10% global import tariff is expected to remain, while discussions focus on modifying the additional 14% reciprocal tariff.
Malaysia, preferring bilateral talks, began official negotiations on May 6. The reciprocal tariff implementation is delayed until July 9, with Malaysia seeking its removal. Small businesses express concerns over the 10% tariff's impact on profit margins, especially in the electronics sector.
IPO Scanner
Stocks to Watch
Bursa Malaysia Securities has raised questions about $GENM (4715.MY)$'s proposed US$41 million acquisition of the remaining 51% stake in Genting Empire Resorts LLC. The regulator seeks clarification on various aspects of the deal, including its rationale, purchase price justification, and financial information on the entities involved. This acquisition would give Genting Malaysia full control of the loss-making Empire Resorts Inc.
$PBBANK (1295.MY)$ plans to increase its dividend payout ratio to 60% in 2025, up from 57% in 2024. CEO Tan Sri Tay Ah Lek announced this at the bank's AGM, noting that dividends remain subject to regulatory approval. The bank expects minimal impact from economic challenges and has implemented prudent lending measures.
$SAPNRG (5218.MY)$ is under MACC investigation for alleged money laundering of over RM500 million in company shares. The probe centers on a prominent "Tan Sri" and covers corruption allegations related to post-merger investments and financial transactions from 2012 to 2021. MACC has raided multiple locations and frozen 83 bank accounts totaling RM158.26 million.
$PENTA (7160.MY)$ reported a 33% decrease in Q1 2025 net profit, dropping to RM13.07 million. Revenue fell 23% to RM131.6 million due to weaker performance in its factory automation solutions division. The company cited macroeconomic uncertainty and geopolitical tensions as factors affecting customer decisions and order book replenishment.
$PAVREIT (5212.MY)$'s Q1 2025 net property income rose 5% to RM142.75 million, driven by higher rental income from Pavilion Bukit Jalil and Elite Pavilion Mall. Gross revenue increased 4.4% to RM228.18 million, with improved occupancy across retail assets. Distributable income reached RM98.16 million or 2.68 sen per unit.
$BJFOOD (5196.MY)$ reported a widened net loss of RM37.19 million in Q3 FY2025, marking its sixth consecutive quarterly loss. The decline was primarily due to weaker performance from Kenny Rogers Roasters operations and ongoing challenges in Starbucks Coffee. Revenue fell 18% to RM113.58 million, reflecting a reduced number of stores in operation.
$GPACKET (0082.MY)$ Bhd has proposed a share capital reduction to offset RM340 million in accumulated losses. The company aims to address its financial position, having recorded consecutive annual losses since 2017. Post-reduction, the group expects to report retained earnings of RM572,000.
$HHRG (0175.MY)$ has dismissed CEO Fong Chee Khuen with immediate effect, citing serious misconduct and abuse of authority. This decision follows Fong's suspension on April 7, 2025, and occurs amid an ongoing dispute between the company's largest shareholder, Cfamillie Holdings Sdn Bhd, and the board over ownership issues related to MG Furniture Sdn Bhd.
$KERJAYA (7161.MY)$ secured a RM162 million contract for a 47-storey transit-oriented serviced apartment project in Johor Bahru. This latest win brings the group's year-to-date new contracts to RM870.3 million, putting it on track to meet its RM1.6 billion annual target. The group's total outstanding order book now stands at RM4.6 billion.

title: For the third consecutive week, there was an Inflow into Malaysian stocks, with foreign investors net buying 0.423 billion last week.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
Kuala Lumpur, 13th – The trend of Inflow from foreign investors has not stopped, with a net purchase of Malaysian stocks amounting to 0.4 billion 22.6 million Ringgit last week, continuing the net buying trend into the third week.
MIDF Research stated in a capital trend report released this week that foreign investors, except for selling 92.4 million Ringgit and 42.4 million Ringgit on Monday and Thursday respectively, bought Malaysian stocks on all other trading days, with Wednesday recording the highest net purchase amount of 0.3 billion 64.8 million Ringgit, followed by Friday's 0.1 billion 35.1 million Ringgit.
However, the net purchase amount from foreign investors last week was lower than the previous week's 0.8 billion 53.8 million Ringgit.
Last week, foreign capital invested in three major sectors: utilities (0.2 billion 53.3 million Ringgit), communications and media (53.3 million Ringgit), and financial services stocks (51.1 million Ringgit).
Only two sectors saw net selling by foreign capital last week, namely energy stocks (-57.5 million Ringgit) and Technology stocks (-56 million Ringgit).
In contrast to foreign capital, local Institutions continued to net sell Malaysian stocks, marking the third consecutive week of selling, with a net sale of 0.3 billion 97.8 million Ringgit in Malaysian stocks.
At the same time, retail investors also continued to act as sellers, with a total net sale of Malaysian stocks amounting to 24.8 million Ringgit last week, although the selling pressure was much less than the previous week's 0.1 billion 61.2 million Ringgit.
In terms of participation, the daily average trading value (ADTV) of foreign investors, local institutions, and retail investors has all increased, by 6.1%, 8.6%, and 2.9% respectively.
The stocks that foreign investors bought the most: $TENAGA (5347.MY)$ , $MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ , $IHH (5225.MY)$ , $GAMUDA (5398.MY)$ , $RHBBANK (1066.MY)$ , $SUNWAY (5211.MY)$ , $GENM (4715.MY)$ , $SDG (5285.MY)$ , $TM (4863.MY)$ , $ECOWLD (8206.MY)$
Most sold stocks by foreign capital: $CIMB (1023.MY)$ , $AMBANK (1015.MY)$ , $DIALOG (7277.MY)$ , $PETGAS (6033.MY)$ , $PCHEM (5183.MY)$ , $HARTA (5168.MY)$ , $IJM (3336.MY)$ , $99SMART (5326.MY)$ , $YINSON (7293.MY)$ , $NATGATE (0270.MY)$

author: Skyrye7
body:
Genting Malaysia Berhad (KLSE: GENM) faces a mixed outlook for 2025, balancing operational recovery with financial headwinds and strategic uncertainties.

📊 Financial Performance & Forecasts
In FY2024, Genting Malaysia reported revenue of RM10.9 billion, up from RM10.2 billion in 2023. Adjusted EBITDA rose to RM2.9 billion, and the company returned to a net profit of RM200 million, reversing a RM400 million loss the previous year .

However, Q4 2024 saw a net loss of RM485.6 million, primarily due to costs associated with its bid for a New York gaming license .

Analysts forecast 2025 revenue at RM11.4 billion , with earnings and EPS expected to grow by 28.2% and 29.2% annually, respectively .

⚠️ Challenges & Risks
Empire Resorts Exposure: Ongoing losses from Empire Resorts in the U.S. continue to weigh on profitability .

Interest & Tax Pressures: Higher interest costs and effective tax rates are expected to keep 2025 earnings 33% below pre-pandemic levels .

Investor Sentiment: Disappointing earnings and rising debt have led to a decline in investor confidence, with shares hitting a five-year low .

🌱 Growth Drivers & Opportunities
Tourism Recovery: The resurgence in domestic tourism supports growth at Resorts World Genting, with Fitch projecting revenue to return to 2019 levels by 2025 .

Strong Core Operations: Despite challenges, Genting Malaysia has surpassed pre-COVID-19 EBITDA levels, indicating robust underlying operations .

Attractive Valuation: The company offers a compelling EV/EBITDA ratio of 5.3x and a dividend yield of 6.7%, appealing to value investors .

🔍 Outlook Summary
While Genting Malaysia is on a path to recovery, challenges such as international losses and financial pressures persist. The company's strong domestic operations and potential for growth in the hospitality sector offer optimism. Investors should monitor developments in its U.S. ventures and broader economic conditions.

author: Lucas Cheah
body:
🎢 What Does the Company Do?
GENM is a Malaysian hospitality and leisure company best known for operating Resorts World Genting — a major integrated resort that includes a theme park, casinos, hotels, shopping, and entertainment.

The company also has international operations, including:
• Resorts World New York City (USA)
• Resorts World Bimini (Bahamas)
• Casinos in the United Kingdom and Egypt

Genting Malaysia is part of the larger Genting Group, a multinational conglomerate involved in leisure, plantations, property, and energy.

💰 How the Company Makes Money

GENM earns revenue primarily from its integrated resorts that combine gaming (casinos), hospitality, retail, and theme parks.

Revenue Streams:
1. Gaming
o Casino operations are the core driver of revenue
o Includes VIP and mass market gaming across Malaysia, the U.S., the U.K., and other regions

2. Hospitality & Leisure
o Hotels, dining, and resort operations in Genting Highlands and overseas

3. Theme Parks, Retail, and Other Services
o Skytropolis Indoor Theme Park and Genting SkyWorlds (outdoor theme park) in Malaysia
o Revenue from ticket sales, food & beverage, and merchandise
GENM is a destination-based business that benefits from tourism, entertainment, and consumer discretionary spending.

📊 What to Watch in Company’s Upcoming Earnings

1. Visitor Numbers and Resort Occupancy
• Track footfall at Resorts World Genting and occupancy rates at hotels
• Tourist return, especially from China and Southeast Asia, is a key growth driver

2. Gaming Revenue Performance
• Watch for YoY growth in casino revenue, especially mass market segments
• Performance of international operations (especially in New York and the U.K.) will also be key

3. Theme Park Revenue (Genting SkyWorlds)
• Genting’s outdoor theme park opened in 2022 and is still scaling
• Uptake in ticket sales, per-guest spending, and operational efficiencies will be watched

4. Cost Control and Margins
• Inflation, energy, and labor costs may affect profitability
• EBITDA margin recovery is a strong signal of operational improvement

5. Debt and Capital Expenditure
• Investors will track capital spending on maintenance and upgrades, especially at Genting Highlands
• Update on leverage and cash flow generation will provide insights into balance sheet health

⚠️ Risks and Challenges

1. High Dependence on Gaming Revenue
• Any drop in gaming activity (due to regulations or competition) could significantly impact earnings

2. Economic Sensitivity
• Resorts and casinos rely on consumer spending and tourism — sensitive to economic downturns, inflation, and geopolitical issues

3. Regulatory Risks
• As a casino operator, GENM is subject to gaming license rules, tax structures, and government oversight in all its operating countries

4. Competition
• Competes with other gaming and resort destinations in Asia (e.g., Macau, Singapore) and online gaming platforms

5. Foreign Exchange and International Exposure
• Overseas earnings are affected by exchange rates, especially from the USD and GBP

🔮 Outlook for 2025

Genting Malaysia is expected to continue its recovery from pandemic-era lows, with more normalized tourism, stronger theme park performance, and stable gaming income.

Key Growth Drivers:
• Full ramp-up of Genting SkyWorlds outdoor theme park
• Stronger international arrivals and tourism support from Visit Malaysia campaigns
• Continued performance improvement in U.S. and U.K. gaming markets
• Potential new licenses or expansion in online gaming or new regions

📌 Summary

Genting Malaysia Berhad is a leading leisure and gaming company in Malaysia and abroad, with its flagship Resorts World Genting being a key destination for tourists and gamblers. The company earns most of its money from casino gaming, but is diversifying through theme parks, hotels, and overseas operations.

For investors, key things to watch:
✅ Casino and hotel performance at Resorts World Genting
✅ Visitor numbers and theme park ticket sales
✅ International contributions (U.S. and U.K.)
✅ Cost control and cash flow
✅ Progress on long-term tourism recovery

GENM is a recovery and reopening story in the broader leisure sector and may appeal to investors seeking exposure to tourism, entertainment, and gaming in Southeast Asia and beyond.

author: CJeng
body:
As of May 2025, Genting Malaysia Berhad (GENM) is facing multiple challenges, leading to pressure on its profitability and market performance. The following are the main adverse factors:

📉 Weak financial performance and declining profits.

Quarterly loss: In the fourth quarter of 2024, GENM recorded a net loss of approximately 0.4856 billion Ringgit, primarily due to a decline in operating profit and an unrealized Forex loss of 356.9 million Ringgit. The full-year core Net income was 0.3877 billion Ringgit, far below the market expectation of around 0.7 billion Ringgit.

Analysts downgrade profit forecasts: Phillip Capital Research has lowered GENM's profit forecast for 2025 to 2027 by 24% to 28% and has reduced the Target Price from 2.60 Ringgit to 1.85 Ringgit, believing the stock may become a 'value trap.'

💸 Rising costs and debt burden.

Increased operating costs: The rise in salary costs in the United States and United Kingdom businesses, as well as upfront expenses related to the bidding for a casino license in New York, have led to a compression of profit margins.

High debt levels: As of now, GENM's total borrowings stand at 12.2 billion Ringgit, of which 60% is denominated in US dollars. It is expected that interest expenses will account for 20% to 22% of adjusted EBITDA between 2025 and 2027, significantly higher than the pre-pandemic level of below 5%.

Recently, Genting significantly reduced the number of dealers due to previous cash flow issues, resulting in a manpower shortage, and will need to rehire contract dealers in July. Additionally, this month, with the new CEO, a renewed focus has been placed on employee meal benefits.

🏢 Operation Challenges and Market Response

Casino renovations impact revenue: The Circus Palace and Hollywood Gambling Zone at Resorts World Genting will be closed for renovations starting February 28, 2024, resulting in a 25% reduction in the projected total Gross Gambling Revenue (GGR) for 2025.
Therefore, this month Genting also launched a new policy where the minimum bet is set at RM100 to reduce low-quality customers and to pay attention to the issue of customers selling houses privately. Additionally, the cable car ticket price has increased from RM10 to RM11 this year, with operations at two locations to boost revenue.

Stock price performance is poor: As of May 2025, GENM's stock price has dropped approximately 21.68% year-to-date and has been removed from the MSCI Malaysia Index, reflecting weakened investor confidence.

⚠️ Downgrade in Ratings and Regulatory Risks

Credit rating downgrade: Standard & Poor's has downgraded GENM's long-term issuer rating from "BBB" to "BBB-" and its standalone credit profile from "bb+" to "bb", primarily due to its weak recovery prospects.

Changes in tax policy: The Malaysian government will increase the service tax rate from 6% to 8% starting March 1, 2024, putting pressure on GENM's profitability.

🧾 Investor Concerns

Dividend reduction: For the fiscal year 2024, GENM announced a full-year dividend of 10 sen per share, down from 15 sen in the fiscal year 2023, reflecting the company's conservative strategy under pressure from capital expenditures and earnings.

Uncertain outlook: Although the recovery of the tourism industry brings some hope, high debt levels, rising operational costs, and changes in the regulatory environment pose challenges to GENM's future profit growth.

In summary, GENM currently faces multiple challenges, and investors should closely monitor its financial performance, operational strategy, and changes in the external environment to assess its long-term investment value.

title: Despite the decline in revenue, Forex gains still boosted Genting Malaysia's profits in the first quarter.
author: 旋风小肥侠
body:
TheEdge
Kuala Lumpur (May 29): Genting Malaysia Berhad (Kuala Lumpur:GENM) for the first quarter ending March 31, 2025, Net income increased by 25.69% year-on-year, benefiting from Forex gains and improved cost management. The group fell into loss in the fourth quarter last year, but Net income increased from 57.78 million Ringgit or 1.02 cents per share a year ago to 72.58 million Ringgit or 1.28 cents per share. Due to weakened contributions from the leisure and hotel businesses in Malaysia and the United Kingdom, as well as the impact of currency conversion, quarterly revenue decreased by 6.14% year-on-year from 2.76 billion Ringgit to 2.6 billion Ringgit. No dividends were declared for this quarter. In this quarter, the Leisure and Hotel Business of Genting Malaysia contributed 2.54 billion Ringgit in revenue, accounting for 97.76% of the Group's total revenue. Its Malaysian Business contributed 1.62 billion Ringgit, a year-on-year decrease of 7%, mainly due to the festive season and a decline in the number of high-end players. Due to unfavorable Forex impacts, revenue from the United Kingdom and Egypt decreased by 7% to 0.4134 billion Ringgit. Meanwhile, revenue from the United States and the Bahamas dropped by 3% to 0.5013 billion Ringgit. The Group stated that although the hotel industry remains optimistic, the 'regional Gambling market may face increasing challenges,' therefore maintaining a cautiously optimistic attitude towards the recent outlook. Its aim is to enhance the appeal of Genting World through new ecotourism products and anniversary celebrations. A significant development includes the acquisition of the remaining 51% stake in Genting Empire Resort LLC for 0.177 billion Ringgit, pending regulatory approval, as the Group prepares for growth in the New York Gambling market. The company added: 'The Group will continue to closely monitor the relevant progress of the application requests to the New York Gambling Facilities Board and is prepared to participate in that process as part of its broader Global Strategy for growth.'

Good morning mooers! Here are things you need to know about today's market:
U.S. Three Major Indexes Inch Higher
Malaysian Stock Market Dips for Fourth Consecutive Day
Bursa Malaysia Partners to Expand Foreign ETF Listings
Stocks to watch: SUNCON, IHH, etc.
- Moomoo News MY
Wall Street Summary
$标普500指数 (.SPX.US)$ 5,912.17 (+0.40%)
$道琼斯指数 (.DJI.US)$ 42,215.73 (+0.28%)
$纳斯达克综合指数 (.IXIC.US)$ 19,175.87 (+0.39%)
U.S. stock indexes edged up slightly on Thursday, responding to the latest twist in the legal saga surrounding President Trump's "Liberation Day" tariffs.
The court ordered the tariffs to be nullified, potentially upending a cornerstone of Trump's trade policy. However, this decision was quickly countered by the U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, which issued a stay on the lower court's ruling.
This temporary suspension means the tariffs will remain in effect while the appellate court conducts a more thorough review of the case.
Investors have consistently welcomed any news that could delay or reduce Trump's tariffs, as evidenced by sharp rises in major stock index futures following the initial court ruling against the tariffs.
This positive market reaction reflects widespread concern among investors about the potential economic fallout from these trade measures. Many fear that the tariffs, combined with foreign retaliation, could lead to higher inflation and unemployment in the US.
The Bureau of Economic Analysis provided a modestly positive update on the U.S. economy Thursday, revising its first-quarter GDP estimate. The new figures show the economy contracted at a 0.2% annual rate, an improvement from the previously reported 0.3% decline.
This slight upward revision, while still indicating economic contraction, offers a glimmer of hope for Wall Street and investors.The adjusted data suggests that the economic slowdown in the first quarter was not as severe as initially thought, potentially signaling more resilience in the U.S. economy than previously believed.
NVIDIA, as the key member of the "Mag-7" stocks, saw its shares climb 3.25% during Thursday's trading session. This significant rise came after the company reported better-than-expected first-quarter earnings and revenues, surpassing analyst estimates.
Conversely, Alphabet and Apple experienced minor declines on Thursday. Alphabet shares dropped 0.29%, while Apple fell 0.23%.
Bursa Market Insight
$富时马来西亚指数 (.KLSE.MY)$ 1518.980 (-0.30%)
Top Gainer: $PETDAG (5681.MY)$ RM20.500 (+1.49%)
Top Loser: $TM (4863.MY)$ RM6.590 (-3.80%)
USD/MYR: $美元/马来西亚令吉 (USDMYR.FX)$ 4.2440 (+0.45%)
The FBM KLCI continued its downward trajectory for the fourth consecutive session, closing 0.3% lower at 1,518.98. This performance stood in contrast to the broader Asian market rally, which was buoyed by a U.S. trade court's decision to block President Trump's tariffs.
Trading was relatively balanced with 466 gainers, 478 losers, and 460 unchanged stocks. The market saw a volume of 3.3 billion shares traded, valued at RM2.22 billion.
Dealers anticipate continued lackluster market conditions in the near term, citing ongoing tariff concerns and a lack of strong domestic catalysts as factors that may keep investors cautious.
Additionally, Bursa Malaysia Bhd, Fullgoal Asset Management (HK) Ltd, and CGS International Securities Malaysia Sdn Bhd have signed a memorandum of understanding to facilitate the listing of foreign-underlying exchange-traded funds (ETFs) on Bursa Malaysia.
This collaboration aims to provide Malaysian investors with access to a wider range of investment options and exposure to global markets.
The agreement, signed at the ASEAN Business Forum 2025, reflects a joint commitment to promote capital market connectivity between China and Malaysia, enrich cross-border product offerings, and enhance the asset management industry's development capabilities.
IPO Scanner
ASM Automation Group Bhd plans to raise RM21.82 million through an IPO on Bursa Malaysia's ACE Market. The company will issue 128.34 million new shares at 17 sen each, representing 24% of its enlarged share capital. Proceeds from the IPO will be used for business expansion in the automation machinery sector.
Stocks to Watch
$SUNCON (5263.MY)$ has secured two significant contracts totaling RM1.16 billion from a leading US technology company. The projects, set to commence immediately and conclude by February 2027, involve general contractor services for data center construction.
$IHH (5225.MY)$ experienced a 33% decrease in net profit for Q1 2025, dropping to RM514 million. This decline was primarily due to accounting adjustments and the absence of a one-time tax credit from the previous year.
$KPJ (5878.MY)$ reported a 20% year-on-year decrease in net profit for Q1 2025, earning RM57.06 million. The decline was attributed to losses in overseas operations and the absence of contributions from discontinued Australian operations.
$GENTING (3182.MY)$ saw a significant drop in net profit for Q1 2025, falling to just RM4.57 million from RM588.87 million a year earlier. This sharp decline was accompanied by a 12.4% decrease in revenue, which totaled RM6.51 billion.
$GENM (4715.MY)$ reported a 25.69% year-on-year increase in net profit for Q1 2025, reaching RM72.58 million. This improvement was primarily due to foreign exchange gains and better cost management.
$CHINHIN (5273.MY)$'s Q1 net profit doubled to RM18.39 million, driven by contributions from Signature International Bhd and a turnaround in its property development segment. Revenue surged 66.9% to RM951.95 million.
$TROP (5401.MY)$ reported a net profit of RM1.32 million in Q1 2025, marking its second consecutive profitable quarter. This result was supported by a tax credit of RM6.63 million. However, quarterly revenue decreased by 10.61% to RM260.36 million due to lower recurring income following property disposals.

title: Heavy selling pressure · a continuous decline. Profit storm stocks face harsh conditions.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 30th) Several listed companies saw their stock prices plummet sharply during the morning trading session due to earnings performance falling short of market expectations, among which, Genting's twin companies became the market focus.
Genting $GENTING (3182.MY)$ On Thursday, it announced a 99% year-on-year decline in net profit for the first quarter of the 2025 fiscal year, significantly below market expectations, causing the stock price to open lower on Friday.
As of noon trading, the stock price plummeted by 3.8% or 12 cents, reaching a low of 3.01 Ringgit for the day, marking a new low since early April.
At the same time, it also dragged down Genting Malaysia. $GENM (4715.MY)$ This morning, it briefly dropped by 1.1% to 1.80 Ringgit, despite recording a 25.6% year-on-year growth in net profit for the first quarter.
This is not the first time Genting has faced a significant drop in stock price due to poor performance. In February this year, Genting announced a loss for the end of the fiscal year 2024, which triggered panic in the market, causing the stock price to plunge nearly 12% the following day.
At that time, Genting Malaysia, which also reported a loss, saw an even greater drop, plummeting 19.5% in a single day, directly falling below the 2 Ringgit level.
Genting is undervalued.
Today, in light of the performance being below expectations, Galaxy International Securities has lowered its earnings forecast and Target Price for Genting to 3.57 Ringgit, but still maintains a 'Shareholding' rating, believing the valuation is undervalued.
Analysts state that the investment logic for Genting remains unchanged and still considers it an effective Indicator for the number of visitors from Malaysia and Singapore.
On the other hand, analysts expect Genting Malaysia to invest higher operating and capital expenditures in the fiscal years 2025 and 2026 for New York's Resorts World (RWNYC) in preparation for the bid for the downstate casino license in New York City, which may lead to a contraction in profit margins and could even reduce dividend payouts.
Therefore, analysts have downgraded the rating for Genting Malaysia from 'Shareholding' to 'Hold' and have cut the Target Price to 1.88 Ringgit.
Ajinomoto Rarely Incurs Losses.
In addition, Ajinomoto $AJI (2658.MY)$ has rarely reported a loss, causing its stock price to drop significantly on Friday, falling as much as 11% or 1.56 Ringgit during the session, reaching 12.68 Ringgit, marking a new low since June 2023.
Ajinomoto reported a loss of 6.9 million Ringgit at the end of the fiscal year 2025 (ending March) mainly due to increased selling and administrative expenses.
Following closely is the Johor Medical Health, which also reported disappointing performance. $KPJ (5878.MY)$ This morning, it once dropped to 2.67 Ringgit, with a decline of 9.8%.
In the first quarter of the 2025 fiscal year (ending March), Johor Medical Health's net profit fell by 20% year-on-year to 57.06 million Ringgit, mainly due to losses in overseas business and the gap left by the cessation of operations in Australia.
Given that the performance in the first quarter only accounted for 16% of the full-year forecast, Hong Leong Investment Bank has revised down the earnings forecasts for the fiscal years 2025 and 2026 by 8.6% and 7.8%, respectively.
Qianli Resources' net profit slows down.
In contrast, Qianli Resources, which has always performed brilliantly, $QL (7084.MY)$ after 11 consecutive quarters of net profit growth, recorded a slowdown in growth for the first time, leading to selling pressure on its stock price, which fell by 2% or 9 cents to 4.45 Ringgit, a relatively light decline.
For the end of the 2025 fiscal year, Qianli Resources earned a net profit of 93.92 million Ringgit, a year-on-year decrease of 4.92%; revenues recorded 1.7 billion 61.4 million Ringgit, with a year-on-year growth of 6.74%.
Analysts from the bank's investment research believe that fishery product manufacturing (MPM) remains a key source of profit in the coming period, but as the egg subsidy will be fully removed on August 1, the profitability of integrated livestock farming (ILF) may weaken due to sluggish prices and increased supply.
Analysts indicated that the net profit for the year only reached 93% of expectations, thus lowering the forecasts for the fiscal years 2026 and 2027 by 11% to 15%.
The net profit of Zhenke plummeted by 96%.
Zhenke, which also fell due to a poor performance report. $GENETEC (0104.MY)$ This morning, it dropped below the Ringgit 1 level, at one point falling 7% to 98.5 cents, hitting a new low in three weeks.
This contract manufacturer of automation industrial equipment saw its net profit in the third quarter of fiscal year 2025 plummet by 96% year-on-year, earning only 0.759 million Ringgit.
Analysts at Galaxy International Securities maintained their 'Shareholding' rating, keeping the Target Price at 81 cents unchanged, considering factors such as the rising client concentration risk, weak global demand for electric vehicles, and the poor demand outlook caused by uncertainties surrounding US tariffs.
Kucingko once plummeted by 18%.
As for the "cat stock" Kucingko company that has been listed for less than a year, $KUCINGKO (0315.MY)$ the financial performance for the first quarter of the 2025 fiscal year was disappointing, and the stock price immediately fell by 18% or 2.5 sen to 11.5 sen on Friday.
This animation company announced its performance on Thursday, with first-quarter revenue plummeting by 97% to 0.21 million Ringgit, and turning from profit to a loss of 3.68 million Ringgit.
Source: Nanyang Siang Pau.

The performance of enterprises in the first quarter has dimmed, market sentiment remains weak, and the Malaysian stock market has seen a continuous decline for half a month since May 15, putting the 1500 support point at risk. On the first trading day of June, the pessimistic sentiment in the Malaysian stock market persists,$FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ The FTSE Bursa Malaysia Composite Index briefly fell below 1500 points during the morning session today, reaching a low of 1497.42 points; however, due to investors taking advantage of the lower prices to buy in, the index was pushed back above the key support level.
Today the morning trading session was closed, the FTSE RINGS index reported at 1503.46 points, down 4.89 points or 0.32%; meanwhile, most Asian stock markets showed an upward trend in the morning. Since the peak of 1586.85 points on May 15, the Malaysian stock market has fallen by 5.26% in half a month. There has only been one day of increase in 13 trading days, and it has now experienced six consecutive declines.
Performance disasters in certain industries. The research analyst at CIMB Investment Bank pointed out that the performance was worse than expected, affecting various Industries, especially in the Oil and Gas, Consumer Goods, Technology, and Bank sectors. As a result, the analyst has revised the core net profit growth forecast for the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI for this year and next year from the original 9.3% and 6.6% down to 3.4% and 6.5%. The index target is 1560. Not only that, analysts have also downgraded the SSE Conglomerates Index target from the original 1657 points to 1560 points. Analysts indicated that there are still multiple downward risks affecting market trends, including uncertainties regarding tariffs, which are expected to continue disrupting the market in the third quarter of this year. Furthermore, the Malaysian government may promote targeted RON95 RBOB Gasoline subsidies within this year and higher electricity charges, therefore, analysts continue to view recent trends with caution. Analysts also pointed out that despite multiple downward risks, there are still Bullish trends worth noting, which may offset the downward factors. These include strong domestic liquidity.$USD/MYR (USDMYR.FX)$ The strengthening of the Ringgit, the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR), the Johor-Singapore XINJINGJI Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), and the New Industrial Master Plan (NIMP 2030) are policies expected to partially mitigate adverse factors.

The research analyst at CIMB Investment Bank pointed out that the performance was worse than expected, affecting various Industries, especially in the Oil and Gas, Consumer Goods, Technology, and Bank sectors.
As a result, the analyst has revised the core net profit growth forecast for the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI for this year and next year from the original 9.3% and 6.6% down to 3.4% and 6.5%.
Not only that, analysts have also downgraded the SSE Conglomerates Index target from the original 1657 points to 1560 points.
Analysts continue to indicate that there are still multiple downward risks affecting the market...

title: How to beat Algorithm Trading?
author: wisepawn
body:
How to beat Algorithm Trading? Disclaimer: The following Q&A is based on AI, use at your own risk.
Beating algorithmic trading, especially high-frequency trading (HFT), is a significant challenge for individual or retail traders due to the immense speed, technological advantage, and capital resources of institutional players. However, it's not entirely impossible to navigate a market dominated by algorithms and even leverage some of their characteristics to your advantage. Here's a breakdown of how to approach it, focusing on understanding algos and developing complementary strategies: 1. Understand the Strengths and Weaknesses of Algorithmic Trading: Strengths of Algos: Speed: Execute trades in microseconds, far exceeding human capability. Emotionless: Make decisions based purely on logic and data, free from fear, greed, or other biases. Consistency: Follow predefined rules without deviation. Data Processing: Can analyze vast amounts of data in real-time. 24/7 Monitoring: Can operate continuously across multiple markets. Efficiency & Lower Costs: Reduce human error and potentially lower transaction costs through optimized execution. Weaknesses of Algos: Lack of Human Judgment/Intuition: Struggle with unexpected events, "black swan" events, or qualitative factors (e.g., political news, sudden shifts in market sentiment not yet reflected in data). Reliance on Predefined Rules: Can be inflexible in rapidly changing or unprecedented market conditions. Technical Vulnerabilities: Prone to system failures, glitches, or data integrity issues. Over-optimization Risk: Strategies fine-tuned to historical data might fail in live markets ("curve-fitting"). High Setup and Maintenance Costs: Significant capital outlay for building and maintaining sophisticated systems. 2. Strategies to "Beat" or Coexist with Algorithmic Trading: Instead of directly competing on speed (which is a losing battle for retail traders against HFTs), the key is to find areas where human attributes or different strategies offer an edge. Focus on Longer Timeframes and Fundamental Analysis: HFTs thrive on short-term, small price discrepancies. Retail traders can focus on longer-term trends, fundamental valuations, and macro-economic factors that algorithms might not fully capture or react to as quickly. This removes you from the direct speed competition. Utilize Human Intuition and Discretion: Humans can interpret news, political events, and market sentiment in a way algorithms currently cannot. Be aware of major news releases or economic reports. Algos might react wildly, but human judgment can discern the long-term implications. Algorithms don't predict market bubbles bursting, but experienced human traders might spot the underlying irrational exuberance. Employ Smart Order Types: Limit Orders: Instead of market orders, use limit orders to ensure your trades are executed at your desired price or better. This protects you from rapid price swings caused by HFTs. Time-Weighted Average Price (TWAP) and Volume-Weighted Average Price (VWAP) strategies: While these are often employed by algos, retail traders can emulate their principles by breaking down larger orders into smaller chunks to minimize market impact, especially for less liquid assets. Look for Less Liquid or Niche Markets: HFTs often concentrate on highly liquid markets with tight spreads. Less liquid or more exotic markets might offer opportunities where the speed advantage of HFT is less pronounced, or where human judgment is more critical. (However, be aware of lower liquidity risks). Understand and Exploit Algorithmic Patterns: Some algorithms operate on identifiable patterns (e.g., trend-following, mean reversion, arbitrage). If you can identify these patterns and anticipate how certain algos might react, you can potentially position yourself to profit. This requires deep market understanding and observation. For example, if you notice an algo consistently sells at a certain resistance level, you might place your sell order just below that level. Leverage Algorithmic Trading Yourself (within your means): While you won't build an HFT system, you can use more accessible algorithmic trading platforms or develop simpler algorithms (e.g., using Python with brokerage APIs). These can help automate your strategies, eliminate emotional biases, and execute trades with more precision than manual trading. Many platforms offer pre-built strategies or low-code/no-code solutions. Backtesting and Optimization: Thoroughly test your own strategies against historical data to ensure their robustness before deploying them live. Risk Management is Paramount: No matter your strategy, robust risk management is crucial. Define clear stop-loss and take-profit levels. Algos can amplify market volatility, so be prepared for rapid price movements. Continuous Learning and Adaptation: The market and algorithmic strategies are constantly evolving. Stay informed about new technologies, market dynamics, and regulatory changes. 3. What NOT to Do: Don't try to beat HFTs on speed: You simply don't have the infrastructure or capital. Don't rely solely on technical indicators without understanding context: Algos can often "spoof" or manipulate technical signals in the short term. Don't trade on emotion: This is precisely where algorithms have an advantage over human traders. In essence, beating algorithmic trading for a retail trader isn't about out-speeding them, but rather about outsmarting them by employing strategies that leverage human strengths and the limitations of automated systems, or by using automated tools to enhance your own trading discipline and efficiency.

title: Foreign capital continues to flee from Malaysian stocks, with a net sale of 0.444 billion last week.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 16th) Foreign capital outflow continues unabated, with a net sale of 0.4 billion Ringgit, slightly higher than the previous week's 0.3 billion Ringgit.
According to the latest Capital Trend report by MIDF Research, foreign investment has been net selling Malaysian stocks on all trading days last week except for Wednesday, with net outflows ranging from 34.6 million Ringgit to 0.2 billion 11.6 million Ringgit.
Among these, the largest single-day outflow occurred on Friday at 0.2116 billion Ringgit, while the net selling on Thursday reached 0.1274 billion Ringgit.
This is the fourth consecutive week of outflow from Malaysian stocks after a brief inflow of foreign investment from the end of April to mid-May.
By sector, the heaviest outflow of foreign capital last week was seen in financial services (-0.3052 billion Ringgit), healthcare (-51.7 million Ringgit), and industrial (-36.8 million Ringgit).
Sectors that attracted foreign investment included industrial products and services (19.4 million Ringgit), Logistics (17.3 million Ringgit), and REITs (8.2 million Ringgit).
The report also pointed out that local Institutions continued as net buyers for the fourth week, recording 0.6 billion 20.6 million Ringgit, while local retail investors have been net selling Malaysian stocks for the second consecutive week, reaching as high as 0.1 billion 76.2 million Ringgit, which is about three times that of the former 57.3 million Ringgit.
Meanwhile, last week's average daily Trade volume showed a situation of "two rises and one fall," with local institutions and retail traders increasing by 12.6% and 14.6% respectively, while foreign investment declined by 8.4%.
The outflow of foreign capital from the top 10 stocks:
$PBBANK (1295.MY)$ , $GAMUDA (5398.MY)$ , $RHBBANK (1066.MY)$ , $AMBANK (1015.MY)$ , $99SMART (5326.MY)$ , $KPJ (5878.MY)$ , $TENAGA (5347.MY)$ , $MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ , $HLBANK (5819.MY)$ , $FRONTKN (0128.MY)$

title: Foreign investment returned to the Malaysian stock market, with a net purchase of 33.2 million last week.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 30th) The position of foreign capital has begun to change, ending a consecutive five-week trend of net selling, and recorded a net buying amount of 33.2 million Ringgit in Malaysian stocks last week.
Overall, the attitude of foreign capital towards the Malaysian stock market remains volatile; according to the latest Capital Trend report from MIDF Research, foreign capital net bought Malaysian stocks on Tuesday and Thursday last week, while net sold on Monday and Wednesday.
Among them, the Inflow amount ranged from 5 million Ringgit to 0.1 billion 44.1 million Ringgit, while the Outflow amount was between 50.7 million Ringgit and 65.2 million Ringgit.
From the sector perspective, last week, the areas favored by foreign investment were utilities (0.1 billion 2.6 million Ringgit), transportation and logistics (45.9 million Ringgit), and industrial products and services (22.9 million Ringgit).
The sectors that experienced the heaviest outflow of foreign investment were finance (0.1 billion 9.9 million Ringgit), industry (35.9 million Ringgit), and telecommunications and media (28 million Ringgit).
The report also pointed out that local institutions continued to net buy Malaysian stocks, extending the net buying trend for the sixth week, recording 0.1 billion 42.8 million Ringgit, down from the previous week's 0.5 billion 10.6 million Ringgit.
Retail investors also turned into net sellers, recording 0.1 billion 76 million Ringgit, ending the net buying trend of the past week.
In addition, besides the average daily trading volume of foreign investment last week, the other two categories saw significant growth, with retail investors and local institutions increasing by 12.7% and 9.7%, respectively, while foreign investment declined by 17.0%.
Foreign investment bought into the top 10 stocks: $MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ , $TENAGA (5347.MY)$ , $ECOSHOP (5337.MY)$ , $WPRTS (5246.MY)$ , $SUNCON (5263.MY)$ , $MYEG (0138.MY)$ , $GENM (4715.MY)$ , $PETDAG (5681.MY)$ , $INARI (0166.MY)$ , $SLVEST (0215.MY)$
Foreign institutions Sold the top 10 stocks: $RHBBANK (1066.MY)$ , $AMBANK (1015.MY)$ , $CIMB (1023.MY)$ , $PBBANK (1295.MY)$ , $TANCO (2429.MY)$ , $YTL (4677.MY)$ , $TM (4863.MY)$ , $YTLPOWR (6742.MY)$ , $GAMUDA (5398.MY)$ , $IHH (5225.MY)$

title: Malaysia Morning Wrap | S&P 500 and Nasdaq Hit Record Highs as US-Canada Trade Dispute Resolves
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Good morning mooers! Here are things you need to know about today's market:
S&P 500 and Nasdaq Hit Record Highs; Canada Scraps Digital Tax Plan
Bursa Malaysia Ends Q2 on Positive Note; Ringgit Strengthens
Stocks to watch: SAPNRG, GENM and etc.
- Moomoo News MY
Wall Street Summary
$标普500指数 (.SPX.US)$ 6,204.95 (+0.52%)
$道琼斯指数 (.DJI.US)$ 44,094.77 (+0.63%)
$纳斯达克综合指数 (.IXIC.US)$ 20,369.73 (+0.47%)
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite reached record highs on Monday, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average also gained. This came as a brief trade dispute between the U.S. and Canada was quickly resolved.
Markets reacted positively after Canada decided not to impose a planned digital-services tax on U.S. tech companies. This decision led President Trump to drop his threats of retaliatory tariffs, and trade talks between the two countries are set to resume.
Investors are now focused on the potential passage of Trump's tax and spending bill in the Senate. While the proposed tax cuts could boost the economy, concerns remain about possible increases in inflation and interest rates due to higher federal deficits.
Bursa Market Insight
$富时马来西亚指数 (.KLSE.MY)$ 1,532.96 (+0.31%)
Top Gainer: $AXIATA (6888.MY)$ RM2.31 (+4.05%)
Top Loser: $KLK (2445.MY)$ RM20.7 (-2.36%)
USD/MYR: $美元/马来西亚令吉 (USDMYR.FX)$ 4.2005 (-0.32%)
The $FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ closed the second quarter with modest gains, rising 0.31% to 1,532.96 points. The index gained 1.3% in Q2 but is down 6.65% for the first half of 2025.
Market breadth was positive, with 531 gainers versus 443 decliners. Trading volume reached 3.57 billion shares, worth RM2.7 billion.
The ringgit hit a one-month high against the US dollar.
Dealers suggest that market gains may remain limited due to cautious investor sentiment and a lack of strong catalysts. Trading is expected to stay range-bound in the near term unless clearer signals emerge.
Malaysia’s six core government-linked investment companies (GLICs) aim to increase the market capitalization of their Bursa Malaysia investments by RM100 billion over five years, targeting a 7.5% annual shareholder return from a RM540 billion portfolio.
Under the expanded GEAR-uP programme, over 30 GLCs will focus on high-growth sectors like semiconductors and energy transition, with RM22 billion already committed for 2025.
Malaysia’s labour market hit a post-pandemic peak in 2024 with a 3.2% unemployment rate and a record 70.6% participation rate, driven by a 3.5% rise in employment to 16.37 million. The outlook for 2025 remains robust, supported by economic growth and Asean initiatives.
IPO Scanner
$UMS (558.SG)$, a Singapore-listed high-precision engineering firm, will pursue a secondary listing on Bursa Malaysia’s Main Market on Aug 1, 2025, to enhance its regional visibility and capitalize on semiconductor and aerospace opportunities.
The listing, supported by TA Securities and CGS International, involves no new share issuance, with fully fungible shares transferable between SGX and Bursa Malaysia.
Stocks to Watch
Bursa Malaysia approved $SAPNRG (5218.MY)$’s regularisation plan to exit PN17 status, including capital and debt restructuring, fundraising, and a general offer exemption. Led by MIDF Amanah, the plan needs shareholder and regulatory approvals.
$SAPNRG (5218.MY)$ Posts RM477.96m Loss in 1QFY2026Sapura Energy Bhd reported a RM477.96 million net loss in 1QFY2026 due to Angola project challenges and higher costs, with revenue falling 31.88% to RM801.37 million.
$GENM (4715.MY)$ bid for a New York casino licence to develop a $5.5 billion resort at Resorts World New York City in Queens. Submitted June 27, a decision is due by December 1, with licences by December 31.
$YINSON (7293.MY)$ will pause major investments to focus on income from projects like the Agogo FPSO. 1QFY2026 net profit fell 43% to RM115 million, revenue to RM1.23 billion. A two-sen dividend is payable on September 26.
$GAMUDA (5398.MY)$ won a RM3.72 billion contract to build a wharf, 2.19km seawall, and 1.2km bridge for Taiwan’s Kaohsiung Port LNG Terminal. The joint venture (70% Gamuda) project is set for completion in five years.
