title: Foreign capital retreated for two consecutive weeks, with an outflow of 960 million ringgit from the Malaysian stock market last week.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 21st) Foreign funds withdrew from the Malaysian stock market for two consecutive weeks, with a total net sell of MYR 962.8 million last week.
According to the fund flow report by M&A Securities Research, foreign funds were net sellers in all five trading days last week, with Monday seeing the highest net sell at MYR 393.5 million.
Foreign funds sold another MYR 320 million worth of Malaysian stocks on Tuesday. Although the outflow slowed subsequently, it accelerated again on Friday ahead of the long weekend, with a single-day net sell of MYR 190 million.
In terms of sectors, the financial services sector saw the largest foreign outflow (-MYR 835.5 million), followed by healthcare (-MYR 270.3 million) and utilities (-MYR 106.7 million).
The sectors that attracted foreign interest were consumer goods and services (MYR 518.9 million), technology (MYR 87.3 million), and construction (MYR 6.5 million).
On the other hand, local institutions continued to support the Malaysian stock market, recording a total net buy of MYR 1.32 billion for the week, extending their net buying streak into the second week.
Local retail investors were net sellers for the sixth consecutive week, with net outflows expanding to MYR 357.4 million, compared to MYR 50.6 million the previous week.
Overall, the average daily trading volume (ADTV) improved slightly last week, primarily due to increases of 26.7% and 18.7% by local retail investors and foreign capital, respectively, while local institutions declined by 4.3%.
Foreign capital flowed out of 10 major stocks: $CIMB (1023.MY)$ , $IHH (5225.MY)$ , $AMBANK (1015.MY)$ , $HLBANK (5819.MY)$ , $MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ , $TENAGA (5347.MY)$ , $PBBANK (1295.MY)$ , $YTLPOWR (6742.MY)$ , $AXREIT (5106.MY)$ , $MISC (3816.MY)$

title: Foreign Outflows Shrink to RM14.6m as Local Institutions Pounce: Malaysia Defies Asia's Capital Outflow Trend
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Hey everyone! Last week saw global markets balancing between growth hopes and inflation worries. While most Asian markets faced foreign outflows, Malaysia told a different story - with local institutions stepping up as foreign investors hesitated.
Market Pulse
Global markets navigated mixed signals as U.S. inflation rose to 3.0% in September, fueling expectations for a Fed rate cut. Solid PMI data (U.S. Composite PMI at 54.8) boosted sentiment, but consumer confidence dipped to 53.6. Most indices rallied, with South Korea's KOSPI leading (+5.14%), while Vietnam and the Philippines lagged. Brent crude jumped 7.6% to USD65.94/barrel, supporting energy sentiment despite lingering policy uncertainties.
Asia's Money Moves
Foreign investors pulled out USD1.74b from Asian markets - the second straight week of outflows! Indonesia led inflows (USD254.7m) after its central bank surprised by holding rates. Thailand saw USD237.4m inflows as its banks pledged accommodative policies. India attracted modest USD96.8m, despite holiday-shortened trading. However, South Korea faced USD593.4m outflows amid rate cut talks, while Vietnam's sell-off extended to 14 weeks!
Malaysia Breakdown
Foreigners sold for the third week, but outflows slowed dramatically to just RM14.6m versus the previous week's RM962.8m. Local institutions bought RM111.1m for their third straight week of purchases. Meanwhile, retail investors sold for the seventh week (RM96.5m outflows). Trading volume fell across the board - foreign participation dropped 25.1%, reflecting a cautious stance.
Stock Spotlight: Who's Buying What?
Foreign Investors' Top Sells:
$IHH (5225.MY)$ (-RM150.1m)
$CIMB (1023.MY)$ (-RM82.3m)
$PBBANK (1295.MY)$ (-RM54.3m)
Local Institutions' Top Buys:
$IHH (5225.MY)$ (RM154.7m)
$PPB (4065.MY)$ (RM69.7m)
$CIMB (1023.MY)$ (RM66.4m)
Local Retail's Top Sells:
$GENM (4715.MY)$ (-RM71.5m)
$MMAG (0034.MY)$ (-RM12.5m)
$INARI (0166.MY)$ (-RM9.6m)
Strategy Breakdown: Why the Divergence?
Local institutions are playing the long game! They've been net buyers for three straight weeks, pumping RM111.1 million into the market. Their strategy? Focus on consumer goods (RM195.7m), industrial products (RM83.0m), and technology (RM66.9m).
Retail investors? They've been selling for seven consecutive weeks! Though outflows slowed to RM96.5m last week, the trend is clear. Trading volume dropped 26.3% - people are sitting on the sidelines.
Foreign Investors continued their selling streak for three weeks, but here's the interesting part: outflows shrank dramatically to just RM14.6m from RM962.8m the previous week! They're still dumping healthcare (RM200.7m) and financial stocks (RM142.7m), but their selling intensity has clearly eased.
Risks to Watch
Watch for local factors: Malaysia's inflation ticked up to 1.5% in September - the highest since February. The Leading Index fell 0.5% yearly, signaling economic softness.
Policy shifts: such as U.S. tariff tensions, may disrupt trade.
Geopolitical risks: such as the Thailand-Cambodia border dispute, add volatility.
Globally: watch for U.S. tariff impacts and central bank surprises. Also monitor oil price volatility after last week's 7.6% surge.

title: Full acquisition of Genting Malaysia poses heavy burden; Fitch may downgrade Genting's rating
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 28th) Due to Genting’s $GENTING (3182.MY)$full acquisition and privatization of Genting Malaysia, $GENM (4715.MY)$this plan has raised concerns from the international rating agency Fitch, as it could increase the financial burden.
According to the latest report, Fitch has placed Genting's long-term Issuer Default Rating (IDR) of 'BBB' on Rating Watch Negative (RWN), indicating that Fitch may downgrade Genting's credit rating in the near future.
In addition to Genting, the bond ratings of its subsidiaries—Genting Malaysia, Genting Overseas Holdings, and Resorts World Las Vegas—have also been placed on negative watch.
Fitch noted that Genting plans to acquire the remaining 50.6% stake in Genting Malaysia for up to MYR 6.7 billion. If a significant number of shareholders accept the offer, this would result in Genting maintaining a high level of leverage over the long term.
"We estimate that Genting's net debt-to-EBITDA ratio could exceed the set sensitivity threshold of 3.5 times after the acquisition, prompting us to consider a downgrade."
Fitch also stated that assuming Genting increases its stake in Genting Malaysia to 60%, the net debt-to-EBITDA ratio would temporarily rise to 3.7 times this year, then gradually decline to 3.4 times in 2026 and 3.1 times in 2027, below the downgrade-triggering threshold of 3.5 times.
"However, if Genting ultimately increases its stake to 66% or higher, the rate of decline in net leverage will slow. In the scenario where Genting holds a larger stake and fully consolidates Genting Malaysia’s earnings, we may adjust Genting's net debt-to-EBITDA ratio to 4.0 times this year, 3.6 times next year, and 3.3 times in 2027."
The agency added that after consolidating earnings, Genting Malaysia is expected to contribute approximately 25% of Genting’s total profits.
New York Gambling License Intensifies Credit Pressure
As Genting's offer price of MYR 2.35 per share represents little premium over Genting Malaysia’s current share price, Fitch stated that it remains uncertain what Genting’s final ownership stake in Genting Malaysia will be.
"Genting may hold a majority stake in Genting Malaysia but may not reach the 75% threshold required for privatization."
Moreover, Fitch pointed out that there is a high likelihood that Resorts World New York, a subsidiary of Genting Malaysia, will secure the new casino license in New York. This could further intensify the credit rating pressures on Genting.
“Genting Malaysia has committed to invest USD 5.5 billion (approximately MYR 23.15 billion), with an initial investment of USD 1.1 billion (approximately MYR 4.63 billion). Currently, we have not incorporated the New York casino license into our baseline forecast.”
The local government of New York will announce the bidding results for the new casino license on December 1.

title: I support the construction of toll stations.
author: 风起云涌LBF
body:
A group of people are taking advantage of Genting's reputation to build apartments and hotels on the mid-slope of Genting (OSK, ASET KAYAMAS, and other developers) and the back slope (NCT), causing the mountain to shake. Lorries carrying sand and gravel have left the roads full of potholes and in a terrible state, with no one maintaining them (the excuse being that they are Genting’s roads).

Well then, it is reasonable that you take advantage of Genting's prosperity. Now, charging tolls for road and infrastructure maintenance is justified (Genting has also experienced frequent landslides due to heavy rains in recent years), which is also a safety consideration.
